</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 70

**Archetype** [Ostilli Host](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=222)

**Prerequisites**
[Ostilli Host Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=5451)

</column>

---

Your ostilli can use its stored magic to protect you from other magic, granting you the Turn Aside Ambient Magic action.

 **Turn Aside Ambient Magic** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561)) Your ostilli glows a faint yellow as it establishes a barrier. Choose acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage. Until the beginning of your next turn, you gain resistance against the chosen damage type equal to half your level.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Deflecting Shot](/Feats.aspx?ID=3183) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 115

**Archetypes** [Sniping Duo](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=121) (Level 12), [Sniping Duo](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=368) (Level 12)

**Trigger**
An ally within the first range increment of your firearm or crossbow is hit by an attack, and you can see the attacker.

**Requirements**
You're wielding a loaded firearm or crossbow.

</column>

---

You're always ready to take a quick shot to deflect a weapon or distract a foe enough to render them off target. The ally gains a +2 circumstance bonus to their AC against the triggering attack. You use this reaction after the result of the attack roll is revealed, so you know whether the +2 will make a sufficient difference.

    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Deflecting Wave](/Feats.aspx?ID=4266) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Water" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=165" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 32

**Trigger**
You would take acid, bludgeoning, fire, or slashing damage from an enemy's attack, spell, or other hostile effect.

**Requirements**
You're aware of the hostile effect, and you aren't [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) against it.

</column>

---

A cascade of water blunts or disperses the incoming attack. You gain resistance to damage from the triggering effect equal to your level if it's bludgeoning or slashing, or double your level if it's acid or fire damage. If the effect deals more than one applicable type of damage, apply the highest resistance, but apply it only once.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Deft Cooperation](/Feats.aspx?ID=873) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=6) pg. 23

**Archetype** [Pathfinder Agent](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=13)

**Prerequisites**
[Pathfinder Agent Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=871)

</column>

---

When you set things up to help your allies, you also gain some of the fruits of your labors. When you successfully [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) an attack roll or AC, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls or AC against that enemy until the end of your next turn, whichever you granted to your ally. When you successfully Aid a skill check, if you attempt the exact same skill check (not just using the same skill, but using it for the same purpose, for instance a check to Climb the same wall) on your next turn, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your skill check.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Defy Chains](/Feats.aspx?ID=8946) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=662" />
<trait label="Sanctified" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=519" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 121

**Archetype** [Nidalese Horselord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=381)

**Prerequisites**
[Nidalese Horselord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8937)

**Trigger**
A fiend within 15 feet of you damages you with a Strike.

</column>

---

You turn to face a fiend that attacked you, looking them squarely in the eyes (if it has them) and showing no fear. You increase the amount of damage you take by 4d6, and deal 4d6 spirit damage to the triggering fiend. The damage you take and deal increases to 5d6 at 18th level.

 In addition, if the fiend has an aura and you're in it, you can attempt an Intimidation check to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the aura's effect, using half your level rounded up as the counteract rank. If you succeed, the effects of the aura are suppressed until the end of the triggering fiend's next turn.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Defy Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=2416) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Orc" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=124" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 50

**Prerequisites**
[Orc Ferocity](/Feats.aspx?ID=83)

</column>

---

You're exceptionally difficult to kill. The DC of your recovery checks is equal to 9 + your dying value, or 8 + your dying value if you have the [Toughness](/Feats.aspx?ID=855) general feat. In addition, whenever someone returns you to life using magic that would normally leave you debilitated for a week (such as [_raise dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=243) or the [resurrect](/Rituals.aspx?ID=20) ritual), you don't suffer that condition.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Defy Fey](/Feats.aspx?ID=4054) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Gunslinger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=406" />
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=136" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 129

**Prerequisites**
[Greenwatch Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=4053)

</column>

---

You are keen to the wiles of the [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69) and can usually shake off their magic. Whenever you fail, but don't critically fail, a save against a spell with a duration of at least 1 round cast by a fey creature, you can attempt a second save against the original DC at the start of your next turn to end any lingering effects the spell might have. This can end [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) caused by a spell but can't reverse any effects that have been resolved already (such as damage dealt when the spell was cast).

<title level="2">Defy Fey leads to...</title>
[Greenwatcher](/Feats.aspx?ID=4058)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Defy Hell](/Feats.aspx?ID=8542) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=701" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #222: Hellbreakers](/Sources.aspx?ID=307) pg. 217, [Hellbreakers Players Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=317) pg. 9

**Archetype** [Hellbreaker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=353)

**Prerequisites**
[Hellbreaker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8534)

**Requirements**
You aren' t [unholy](/Traits.aspx?ID=521).

</column>

---

Your devotion to your cause gives you endless strength and courage to withstand the enemy's attacks. As long as you're in this stance, you gain a +2 status bonus to saves against [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) effects and can make Hellbreaker Strikes.

**Hellbreaker Strike** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([holy](/Traits.aspx?ID=517)) Make a weapon or unarmed Strike. This counts as two attacks when determining your multiple attack penalty. If your Strike hits, you deal an additional 2d8 spirit damage. At 18th level, this increases to 3d8 spirit damage.

---

Using ancient dwarven methods developed to fight enemies wielding magical darkness, you've honed your darkvision and sworn not to use such magic yourself. You gain [greater darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), enabling you to see through magical darkness even if it normally hampers darkvision (such as the darkness created by a 4th-level [_darkness_](/Spells.aspx?ID=59) spell). You can't cast spells with the [darkness](/Traits.aspx?ID=39) trait, use item activations with the darkness trait, or use any other ability with the darkness trait.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 127

**Archetype** [Eternal Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=292)

**Prerequisites**
[Eternal Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7374)

</column>

---

You make a forceful attack that has the power to push your foe through walls. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) and make a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) at mythic proficiency. If you hit and deal damage to the target, you push them up to 15 feet away from you. If this movement would cause the target to collide with an object that has a [hardness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2183) of 5 or less, the object [breaks](/Conditions.aspx?ID=60) and the target is pushed through the object’s space for the remainder of the [forced movement](/Rules.aspx?ID=2364), taking an additional 2d6 bludgeoning damage (the GM can decide that this is a different type of damage depending on the object the target was pushed through; for instance, slashing damage is the target is pushed through a pane of glass). If the forced movement doesn’t cause the target to collide with an object, the target must succeed at a Reflex saving throw against your class DC or be knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88) at the end of the movement.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Demolition Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=1594) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=7" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 106

**Archetypes** [Demolitionist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=118) (Level 4), [Demolitionist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=365) (Level 4)

</column>

---

You can rig your bombs to inanimate objects in order to cause destruction to the surrounding area. As an activity that takes 1 minute, you attach between one and four bombs to an inanimate object within your reach, such as a chest, door, wall, or column. This creates a hazard in one square occupied by or adjacent to the inanimate object, and the hazard's [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) DC to detect it and [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC to disable it are equal to your class DC. The hazard has the following reaction, which you can also trigger as a single action so long as you are within 30 feet of the hazard. The hazard retains its potency until it's triggered, until the inanimate object moves from its space, or until you make your next daily preparations, whichever comes first.

**Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> Fire in the Hole;   **Trigger** A creature moves into the hazard's space;  **Effect** The hazard explodes, dealing the bombs' damage and splash damage to the inanimate object. Combine this damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses, and this damage ignores an amount of the object's Hardness equal to your level. Any creatures adjacent to the hazard take the bombs' splash damage, similarly combined for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses. As a reminder, since you didn't throw the bombs, Calculated Splash and similar effects don't apply.

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 133

**Archetype** [Demolitionist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=118)

</column>

---

You know how to set explosives to cause the maximum possible damage to buildings and other structures. You become trained in [Engineering Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) or become an expert in it if you were already trained. You gain the Set Explosives action.

 **Set Explosives** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Requirements** You have 1 or 2 [bombs](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=7) in hand; **Effect** You attach the bombs to an inanimate object within your reach, such as a door, wall, or column, and rig them to detonate at a set time. The bombs explode at a specific time you determine (such as after your next action or at the start of your next turn, to a maximum of 1 minute), dealing their damage and splash damage to the inanimate object. Combine this damage for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses, and this damage ignores an amount of the object's Hardness equal to your level. Any creatures adjacent to the hazard take the bombs' [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) damage, also combined for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses. As a reminder, since you didn't throw the bombs, the [bomber research field field discovery](/ResearchFields.aspx?ID=8) and similar effects don't apply. Making sure your timing is correct requires concentration, so you can't Set Explosives again while you're waiting for a previously set bomb to detonate.

<title level="2">Demolitionist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Collapse Wall](/Feats.aspx?ID=3244), [Controlled Blast](/Feats.aspx?ID=3243), [Explosive Entry](/Feats.aspx?ID=3242), [Safety Measures](/Feats.aspx?ID=3241)

Making sure your timing is correct requires concentration, so you can’t Set Explosives again while you’re waiting for a previously set bomb to detonate. Special You can’t select another dedication feat until you’ve gained two other feats from the demolitionist archetype. Demolitionist Dedication leads to... Collapse Wall, Controlled Blast, Explosive Entry, Safety Measures

The [demons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387) of Tanglebriar have long haunted your dreams, just as they have long threatened Kyonin. You have not only studied these fiendish foes well, but have trained extensively to battle the hordes of demons that serve [Treerazer](/Deities.aspx?ID=324) and are particularly adept at striking desperate melee blows against them. 

When you make your daily preparations, choose one kind of demon, such as [succubus](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2897), [omox](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2898), [shemhazian](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2900), or Treerazer. At 13th level, the extra damage increases to 2d6 additional spirit damage, and at 17th level, the extra damage increases to 3d6 spirit damage.

>
[Demon's Hair](/Feats.aspx?ID=2746) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Fists of the Ruby Phoenix</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #168: King of the Mountain](/Sources.aspx?ID=87) pg. 75

**Prerequisites**
[Living Hair](/Feats.aspx?ID=1570)

</column>

---

Your hair constantly wriggles and writhes like that of your rival, Syu Tak-nwa. Your damage die of your hair unarmed Strike increases by one step and it gains the [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192) and [versatile slashing](/Traits.aspx?ID=200) traits. Your familiar assumes partial control over your hair; as long as your familiar is alive and within 30 feet, you are permanently [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=32), and you can use the extra action only to make a hair Strike. You can deliver [hexes](/Traits.aspx?ID=324) through your hair. When you successfully cast a non-cantrip hex that requires 2 or more actions to cast and that doesn't require a spell attack roll, if your target is within your reach, as part of the spellcasting activity you can make a hair Strike against them before applying any effects of the hex. If this Strike misses, the hex has no effect.

**Special** If your hair already has the reach trait, it instead gains the [sweep](/Traits.aspx?ID=194) trait.

<title level="2">Capstone Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #168: King of the Mountain](/Sources.aspx?ID=87) pg. 75

Player characters can select one of the following new class feats for their 20th-level class feat upon entering the _Glass Lighthouse_ or by meditating on the cushion in area H4.

**Related Feats**: [All the Time in the World](/Feats.aspx?ID=2744), [Dance of Intercession](/Feats.aspx?ID=2745), [Everdistant Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=2747), [Extradimensional Stash](/Feats.aspx?ID=2748), [Head of the Night Parade](/Feats.aspx?ID=2749), [Heart of the Kaiju](/Feats.aspx?ID=2750), [Plum Deluge](/Feats.aspx?ID=2751), [Ruby Resurrection](/Feats.aspx?ID=2752), [Scapegoat Parallel Self](/Feats.aspx?ID=2753), [Sever Space](/Feats.aspx?ID=2754), [Time Dilation Cascade](/Feats.aspx?ID=2755), [Vitality-Manipulating Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=2756), [Vivacious Afterimage](/Feats.aspx?ID=2757), [Whirlwind Toss](/Feats.aspx?ID=2758), [Worldsphere Gravity](/Feats.aspx?ID=2759)

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 72

**Prerequisites**
[healing font](/Classes.aspx?ID=5)

**Trigger**
Any ally within 30 feet that you can heal with your _heal_ spell would take damage from an attack or effect from a source you can observe.

**Requirements**
You have a [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) spell prepared and you aren't [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) to the source of the damage.

</column>

---

You can manipulate the same energies that the _aeon orbs_ use to sustain life. You cast _heal_ on the triggering target. Instead of its normal effects, the _heal_ spell reduces the triggering damage by an amount equal to the Hit Points a 1-action _heal_ spell of that level would have recovered. As usual, if this reduces the damage to 0, it might also remove additional effects of the triggering attack, such as [injury](/Traits.aspx?ID=97) poisons.

Attempt a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) check and compare the result to the Will DCs of up to three of the triggering creature's allies within 30 feet of you. If you succeed on the check, the target refuses to treat the triggering creature as an ally for 1 round (2 rounds on a critical success). It's possible to get a different degree of success for each target. If you're a master in Diplomacy, you can instead target up to five creatures, and if you're legendary in Diplomacy, you can target up to 10 creatures.

When you succeed or critically succeed at a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) check to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48) an opponent, that target can't flank with their allies until the beginning of your next turn.

<title level="2">Gang Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #159: All or Nothing](/Sources.aspx?ID=48) pg. 75

Street gangs in Absalom recruit amateur pickpockets, ruffians, and vandals who show promise in their specialties and operate well in tight groups.

 Rogue agents can gain access to some of the following rogue feats by successfully helping Maurrisa Jonne or Bloody Berleth eliminate their rival (see Chapter 1). Some of these feats, however, can be gained only by helping a particular side in the gang conflict.

---

A vortex of sand and dust surrounds you. Each creature inside your kinetic aura (including you) is [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) from any creature outside your kinetic aura, and creatures outside the aura are concealed from creatures inside the aura other than you. Your air impulses carry sands that cut at great speed. When you use a damaging air [impulse](/Traits.aspx?ID=502) that affects at least one creature in your kinetic aura, that impulse deals 1 additional slashing damage, or 2 if the impulse has a single target.

---
**Level (+2)** The extra damage increases by 1, or 2 if the impulse has a single target.

</title>

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />

**Prerequisites**
[Mummy Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3520)

---

You draw in the moisture from nearby creatures, draining them dry to heal your wounds. Creatures in a 30-foot cone take 6d8 negative damage, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. A creature that critically fails this saving throw is also [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10). As long as at least one creature was damaged by your Desiccating Inhalation, you regain HP equal to your level.

 At 14th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d8.

<trait label="Healing" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=89" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
</traits>

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 34

**Prerequisites**
[Officer's Medical Training](/Feats.aspx?ID=7795); Master in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42)

**Requirements**
You are holding a [healer's toolkit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2727) or are wearing one and have a free hand; the target's body is mostly intact; the target was not killed by a death effect.

</column>

---

You can use your training in combat medicine to revive the recently deceased. Attempt a DC 40 [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=42) check to revive a dead creature that has been dead for no more than 3 rounds. If you succeed, the target returns to life with the effects of raise dead, except it still has the [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=99) condition it had before dying, increased by 1 (or wounded 1 if it wasn't wounded before dying). Whether you succeed or fail, the target is temporarily immune to Desperate Resuscitation for 1 day.

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 40 **Usage** imbued into a worn ikon --- You demand a battle against your chosen enemy. The imbued ikon gains the following abilities. **Immanence** Whenever an enemy successfully Strikes you with a melee weapon, you gain a +2 status bonus to your AC against the next attack from that enemy before the start of your next turn.
**Transcendence—Only You and I** (concentrate, transcendence) You draw your foe into a fated conflict—one you know you’ll win. Choose an enemy within your reach. Until the end of your next turn, that enemy gains a +2 circumstance bonus to attack rolls it makes against you, but it must attempt a Will save against your class DC whenever it tries to move away from you, Strike a target other than you, or Cast a Spell that doesn’t include you as a target. You can protect yourself more effectively, at the expense of your shield. When you [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839), you can reduce the damage to yourself by double the shield's Hardness, but if you do, the shield takes double the normal amount of damage it would have taken (before applying its Hardness). You can't use Destructive Block if your shield can't be broken or destroyed, such as if you're using an [_indestructible shield_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=322).

<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 152

**Archetype** [Eagle Knight](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=314) (Level 16)

**Frequency**
once per day

</column>

---

Your training allows you to shrug off your foes' spells and conditions when the need is dire. Choose a single nonpermanent spell or condition that is affecting you. If you chose a condition, its effect on you ends. If you chose a spell, attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the spell (your counteract level is equal to half your level, rounded up, and you attempt a Will save as your counteract check).

 This doesn't remove any Hit Point damage normally dealt by the spell or condition, and it doesn't prevent the spell or debilitating effect from affecting other allies or the environment around you. It can't remove an ongoing affliction or prevent such an affliction from inflicting conditions on you later. It can't remove conditions from the situation (such as [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) or flanked). If the effect comes from a creature, hazard, or item of 20th level or higher, Determination can't remove its effect on you.

You can attempt an Athletics check instead of an Acrobatics check to Balance when moving across narrow surfaces or uneven ground, using the same DC. This doesn't prevent you from being harmed by hazardous terrain. You can increase the number of actions this activity takes to 3 to Stride three times instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Determined Lore Seeker](/Feats.aspx?ID=2239) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 45

**Archetype** [Scrollmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=31)

**Prerequisites**
[Lore Seeker](/Feats.aspx?ID=1131)

</column>

---

You've mastered useful spells that let you find hidden truths others might miss, and a preferred spell comes naturally to you. When you gain this feat, choose one of the innate spells granted by the [Lore Seeker](/Feats.aspx?ID=1131) feat: [_comprehend language_](/Spells.aspx?ID=46), [_restore senses_](/Spells.aspx?ID=259), or [_see invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=271). You can cast this spell three times per day instead of once per day.

 When you cast any of the spells granted by Lore Seeker as innate spells, they gain additional effects. When you cast _comprehend language_, the spell is heightened to 4th level. When you cast _restore senses_, the spell is heightened to half your level, rounded up. When you cast _see invisibility_, for the duration of the spell you can use an action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait, to see invisible creatures normally (instead of seeing them as translucent shapes that are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) to you) until the end of your next turn.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 98

**Archetype** [Soulforger](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=393)

**Prerequisites**
[Soulforger Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=9350)

**Requirements**
At least one of your soulforged armaments is not manifested.

</column>

---

Your armaments are especially powerful the moment after you manifest them. You Manifest Soulforged Armament. If you manifested a weapon, make up to two [Strikes](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) with that weapon, each targeting a different creature and each dealing an additional 1d6 spirit damage. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but your penalty doesn’t increase until you have made all your attacks. If you Manifested an armor or shield, you gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 5 to all damage until the start of your next turn. If you manifested both a weapon and an armor or shield, you gain both effects.

    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Devastating Weaponry](/Feats.aspx?ID=3085) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 31

**Prerequisites**
[weapon innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=3)

</column>

---

You release a volley of projectiles from your weapon, or power it to fly in every direction across the battlefield and Strike multiple creatures. Make a Strike with your weapon innovation against each foe within 30 feet of you. Don't increase your multiple attack penalty until after making all the attacks. If your innovation is a melee weapon and any of the attacks are outside your reach, you Release the weapon before the Strikes, and it returns to your grasp after all of them. If your hands are full when the weapon returns, it falls to the ground in your space. As normal, if your weapon innovation requires one or more actions to [reload](/Traits.aspx?ID=254) between Strikes, you can't use it to make multiple attacks with Devastating Weaponry.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 62

</column>

---

You've learned to draw your fiendish nature into a small ball of corruption and hide it in your soul. Your obviously fiendish traits disappear, including any tails, horns, and cloven hooves, though hints remain (claws turn into jagged nails or eyes retain an odd hue, for instance). You're still recognizably yourself, but now appear as a typical, non-tiefling member of your base ancestry. Using Devil in Plain Sight counts as creating a disguise when using [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46), and your transformation automatically defeats Perception DCs to determine if you're a normal member of your base ancestry; only creatures actively rolling Perception to examine you might notice the disguise. While in your shapeshifted form, you can't use unarmed attacks, innate spells, or other abilities that require physical features you receive from a tiefling ancestry feat—for instance, you can't use the [Skillful Tail](/Feats.aspx?ID=1386) feat. You can remain in your alternate form indefinitely, and can shift back to your tiefling form by using this action again.

<title level="2">Devil in Plain Sight leads to...</title>
[Finest Trick](/Feats.aspx?ID=2457)

---

Your knowledge of your enemies gives you an advantage against them, granting you a swift reaction to their devilry. If you know you're fighting against any devils or Hellknights at the beginning of an encounter, you can roll the respective [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=41) skill for your initiative roll.

 In addition, whenever you successfully [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2367) about a creature using Devil Lore or Hellknight Lore, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your next skill check against that creature before the end of your next turn. If you're a master in Devil Lore or Hellknight Lore, the bonus increases to +2.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Human" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=90" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 11

</column>

---

You know more about the habits of devils than is entirely safe. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks against [devils](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30) and saving throws against their abilities. In addition, whenever you meet a devil in a social situation, you can immediately attempt a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) check to Make an Impression on that creature rather than needing to converse for 1 minute. You take a –5 penalty to the check. If you fail, you can engage in 1 minute of conversation and attempt a new check at the end of that time rather than accepting the failure or critical failure result.

**Special** If you have the [Glad-Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=787) skill feat, you don’t take the penalty to your immediate Diplomacy check if the target is a devil.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Devil's Eye](/Feats.aspx?ID=3749) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 55

**Prerequisites**
You made a bargain with a [devil](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30) or won a legal case or other similar duel of wits against a devil.

</column>

---

Your experience in the finer points of bargaining with a devil has awakened a sinister power that now inhabits your left eye. The eye is the same shape and iris color as your normal eye would be, but the sclera is a deep red instead of white and the pupil is a narrow, vertical slit. The eye grants you an abnormal understanding of the loopholes and legal processes employed to trap poor creatures that don't know any better. You gain the Objection reaction. You also become an expert in [Legal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to any check you make to read or negotiate a treatise, contract, or similar text. At 7th level you become a master of Legal Lore, and at 15th level you become legendary in Legal Lore. You can use Legal Lore in place of Perception to detect verbal loopholes, double entendres, hidden meanings, code, or contradictions in a conversation you can hear. This doesn't let you fully understand coded speech but alerts you to its presence.

 **Objection** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76)) **Frequency** once per minute; **Trigger** You're about to attempt a saving throw against a [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101) effect; **Effect** Your devil's eye crackles with infernal glee as you discover a loophole in the wording of the triggering effect. You roll your saving throw twice, taking the higher result.

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 78 _[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) The Critical Success effect of Devrin’s Cunning Stance to deny an enemy’s reaction only applies if an ally’s Strike is successful against a flat-footed enemy._ **Archetype** [Marshal](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=254) **Prerequisites** [Marshal Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2005); Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) **Access** Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat. --- You've learned Devrin Arlos's guileful ways, and his sly teachings help you remind your allies to keep their wits about them. When you use this action, attempt a Deception check. The DC is usually a [standard-difficulty DC of your level](/Rules.aspx?ID=554), but the GM can assign a different DC based on the circumstances. The effect depends on the result of your check. **Critical Success** Your marshal's aura increases to a 20-foot emanation, and it grants you and your allies a +1 status bonus to skill checks. When you or an ally in the aura successfully Strike a [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) enemy, that enemy can't use reactions until the beginning of its next turn.
**Success** As critical success, but your aura's size doesn't increase.
**Failure** You fail to enter the stance.
**Critical Failure** You fail to enter the stance and can't take this action again for 1 minute.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Rogue" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=139" />
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=321" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Firebrands](/Sources.aspx?ID=196) pg. 76

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5)

**Access**
Members of the Firebrands at the rank of second mark or higher have access to this feat.

</column>

---

Devrin Arlos has a habit of using whatever is at hand to temporarily blind others in combat. Copying his technique, you make use of your cloak, the light reflecting from your weapon, a handful of flower petals, or some other physical distraction as part of your feint, leaving your opponent unable to see for a moment. When you successfully [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48) a creature, it becomes [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) until the end of your turn. If you critically succeed, the creature is dazzled until the start of your next turn. The creature can use an Interaction to remove the dazzled condition. As normal, you can dazzle only creatures that use vision or a similar sense, as determined by the GM.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Different Worlds](/Feats.aspx?ID=923) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 73

**Prerequisites**
ability to select ancestry feats from multiple ancestries

</column>

---

Your separate experiences in different societies have evolved into entirely separate lives. Create a second identity for yourself with a different name, history, and background. This identity must correspond to one of the ancestries whose ancestry feats you can select. You gain the trained proficiency rank in the Lore skill from the second background you chose (but you don’t gain any of the background’s other benefits), and you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks when making a statement that would be true of your second identity or when disguising yourself as your second identity.

<title level="2">Lacunafex Lore</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #147: Tomorrow Must Burn](/Sources.aspx?ID=8) pg. 72

If the PCs earn Mialari Docur's trust and prove their worth by defeating the Scarlet Triad, she rewards them by granting them access to several feats and spells she and her students have developed over the years.

**Related Feats**: [Reveal Machinations](/Feats.aspx?ID=924), [Secret Speech](/Feats.aspx?ID=925), [Silver's Refrain](/Feats.aspx?ID=926), [Tweak Appearances](/Feats.aspx?ID=927)

    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Dig Quickly](/Feats.aspx?ID=1214) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Shoony" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=296" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #153: Life's Long Shadows](/Sources.aspx?ID=29) pg. 72

**Requirements**
You are standing on dirt, sand, snow, or similar particulate material.

</column>

---

Your hands work as effectively as shovels when you need to dig a quick hole. You dig a shallow pit in the square you currently occupy, turning the square into difficult terrain (including for you). In addition, you also kick up a cloud of grit in a direction of your choice. The cloud extinguishes small, unattended, non-magical fires and helps smother the flames on burning creatures located within the cone; creatures in this cone that are taking [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) can immediately attempt an additional flat DC 15 check to end the persistent damage.

<title level="2">Dig Quickly leads to...</title>
[Sodbuster](/Feats.aspx?ID=1224)

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**
[_dimensional assault_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1037) focus spell, [laughing shadow hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=2)

</column>

---

You take advantage of teleportation to better hide your position. When you cast [_dimensional assault_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1037), you're affected by an [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=164) spell at the end of the teleport. You can choose not to make the Strike that is normally part of _dimensional assault_. If you do make the Strike, your invisibility ends after the Strike, as normal for _invisibility_.

</title>

---

You can lob bombs with great force and a precise trajectory to angle the splash in a cone spraying in a single direction. When throwing an alchemical bomb with the [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=150) trait, instead of splashing all squares adjacent to the target, you can treat the target’s space as the first affected square of a 15-foot cone directed away from you, potentially allowing you to avoid allies and splash deeper into enemy lines. If the target takes up more than a single square, the target’s square closest to you is the first affected square of the cone.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Battlecry!](/Sources.aspx?ID=268) pg. 43

**Prerequisites**
[Intercept Attack](/Actions.aspx?ID=3305)

**Trigger**
You Intercept an Attack that was made with a melee weapon by a creature you’re adjacent to.

</column>

---

When you catch a weapon in your armor, you can move your body to wrench it from your foe's grasp. After [Intercepting the Attack](/Actions.aspx?ID=3305), attempt to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=2383) the weapon used for that attack. You don't need to have a hand free, and you gain an item bonus to the Athletics check equal to the value of your armor's potency rune.

You attempt a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) check against the triggering attacker's Will DC. You can begin talking to the creature on your next turn to attempt another Diplomacy check; on a success, you sustain the effect until the beginning of your next turn, to a maximum of 1 minute. Talking on subsequent rounds requires that you be able to communicate with the target creature and imparts the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) and [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101) traits to the action.
**Success** Your foe pauses momentarily. Their attack fails, but they can attempt further attacks against you.
**Failure** The target's attack is unaffected. Disarming Smile leads to... [Emphatic Emissary](/Feats.aspx?ID=4120)

[Disarming Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=380) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fighter" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=71" />
<trait label="Stance" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=152" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 147

**Archetypes** [Duelist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=58) (Level 8), [Duelist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=248) (Level 8)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)

**Requirements**
You are wielding only a single one-handed melee weapon and have your other hand or hands free.

</column>

---

You adopt a fencing stance that improves your control over your weapon. While you are in this stance, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) and a +2 circumstance bonus to your Reflex DC when defending against checks to Disarm you. In addition, you can attempt to Disarm creatures up to two sizes larger than you.

<trait label="Press" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=133" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 150

**Archetypes** [Duelist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=58) (Level 12), [Duelist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=248) (Level 12)

Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3)

**Requirements**
You are wielding only a single one-handed melee weapon and have your other hand or hands free.

</column>

---

After your initial attack redirects your foe's defenses, your follow-up wrests their weapon from their grasp. Make a melee Strike with the required weapon. In addition to its other effects, this Strike gains the success and critical success effects of the [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=41) action. The Strike also has the following failure effect.

**Failure** The target is flat-footed until the end of your current turn.

>
[Discerning Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=2274) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 119

**Archetype** [Pathfinder Agent](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=13)

**Prerequisites**
[Pathfinder Agent Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=871); [Thorough Reports](/Feats.aspx?ID=874)

**Requirements**
You have successfully identified the target with [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) during this combat.

</column>

---

Identifying a creature is the first step in finding its weaknesses. Attempt a Strike against the target; if successful, you deal an additional 1d6 precision damage. If you have succeeded on a Recall Knowledge check against the target during this combat and their creature type was previously recorded using [Thorough Reports](/Feats.aspx?ID=874), you also deal 1 point of [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). The creature is then temporarily immune to Discerning Strike for 1 day.

<title level="2">Swords Training</title>

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 119

Marcos Farabellus (_Lost Omens Pathfinder Society Guide_ page 50) is a talented swordsman and likely the most beloved of the Society's three deans. In addition to teaching his students about the dangers of exploring ruins through energetic and performative lectures, Farabellus also teaches his favorite students a few of the martial techniques he's developed over his illustrious career. The Farabellus Flip is a class feat for barbarians, fighters, or rangers. When you select the feat, it loses the traits from the other classes.

**Related Feats**: [Farabellus Flip](/Feats.aspx?ID=2275)

[Disk Rider](/Feats.aspx?ID=3378) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_floating disk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=124)

</column>

---

When you cast _floating disk_, you can modify its duration to be sustained, up to 10 minutes. If you do, add the following heightened entry to its effects.

**Heightened (3rd)** The disk can hold up to 10 Bulk. The spell no longer ends if you ride atop the disk (though it does if any other creature rides atop it, including if the creature is riding on you). If you are riding the disk, it changes its capacity to hold you, plus additional Bulk equal to the maximum you could carry without being [encumbered](/Conditions.aspx?ID=12). If you ride atop the disk, you can direct it to move along the ground up to 30 feet or your Speed, whichever is slower, each time you Sustain the Spell. While you ride atop it, the disk can move over liquids as long as it ends its movement on solid ground. If it ends its movement on a surface that can't support it, the spell ends.

>
[Dismounting Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=8942) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 121

**Archetype** [Nidalese Horselord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=381)

**Prerequisites**
[Nidalese Horselord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8937)

**Requirements**
You are mounted on your horse, and your last action was to [Command an Animal](/Actions.aspx?ID=2400) to order your horse to Stride at least once.

</column>

---

You leap from your horse, using the momentum of its movement to deal a devastating blow with your melee weapon. You use the [Mount](/Actions.aspx?ID=2314) action to dismount your horse but can move to any space within 10 feet of your mount, as long as your horse moved at least 15 feet. You then make a melee Strike. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. If this Strike hits, you deal an extra die of weapon damage. If you're at least 14th level, increase this to two extra dice.

fields.text: Feat 8 Dismounting Strike Single Action Archetype Source Hellfire Dispatches pg. 121 Archetype Nidalese Horselord Prerequisites Nidalese Horselord Dedication Requirements You are mounted on your horse, and your last action was to Command an Animal to order your horse to Stride at least once. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 49

**Prerequisites**
[Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

**Requirements**
Your Spellstrike is charged.

</column>

---

The spell you deliver tries to force out magic affecting your enemy. Make a Spellstrike. If it hits, you also attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) a single spell (of your choice) active on the target. The counteract level is half your level rounded up, and the counteract check modifier is the standard modifier for counteracting with a spell (your Intelligence modifier plus your spellcasting proficiency bonus, plus any bonuses or penalties that specifically apply to counteract checks).

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Disperse into Petals](/Feats.aspx?ID=7633) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Wardens of Wildwood</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Deviant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=426" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Plant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=125" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=127" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #202: Severed at the Root](/Sources.aspx?ID=242) pg. 75

</column>

---

You merge with the blossoms sprouting from you and disperse, becoming a visible cloud of blossoms and petals. You’re amorphous. You lose any item bonus to AC and all other effects and bonuses from armor, and you use your proficiency modifier for unarmored defense. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to physical damage equal to half your level and are immune to precision damage. You can’t cast spells, activate items, or use actions that have the attack or [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait. You gain a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) of 10 feet. You can remain in this form for up to 1 minute. You can [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) this effect.

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

---

The slightest distraction can provoke your wrath, and you're prepared to foil enemies' actions. As long as you are in this stance, you can use [Attack of Opportunity](/Actions.aspx?ID=8) when a creature within your reach uses a [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) action, in addition to [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) and [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) actions. Furthermore, you [disrupt](/Rules.aspx?ID=394) a triggering concentrate or manipulate action if your Strike hits (not only if it's a critical hit).

>
[Distant Wandering](/Feats.aspx?ID=3791) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Deviant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=426" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gatewalkers Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=190) pg. 11, [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 103

</column>

---

Your body falls [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) and your spirit projects out of it. While in spirit form, you can't consciously move your body, and you are [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) and inaudible, though a creature still might notice the signs of your presence and passing, just like for an invisible creature affected by [_silence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=287), or a [_prying eye_](/Spells.aspx?ID=239). You can freely move about, though you can't touch or move anything, cast spells, attack, or otherwise affect anything around you. Despite your ghostly form, you are not [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) and can't pass through barriers you couldn't in your body. Most effects can't harm your spirit form, though some spells, like [_spirit blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=301) and [_spirit song_](/Spells.aspx?ID=303), explicitly damage a creature's spirit. You can return to your body as a free action. If you are in spirit form at the beginning of your turn, you must attempt another backlash check for your deviation, returning to your body if you fail.

[Distant Wandering](/Feats.aspx?ID=8045) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Deviant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=426" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gatewalkers Player's Guide (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=287) pg. 13, [Dark Archive (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=293) pg. 103

</column>

---

Your body falls unconscious and your spirit projects out of it. While in spirit form, you can’t consciously move your body, and you are [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=83) and inaudible, though a creature still might notice the signs of your presence and passing, just like for an invisible creature affected by [_silence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1674), or a [_scouting eye_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1661). You can freely move about, though you can’t touch or move anything, cast spells, attack, or otherwise affect anything around you. Despite your ghostly form, you are not [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=632) and can’t pass through barriers you couldn’t in your body. Most effects can’t harm your spirit form, though some spells, like [_spirit blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1685) and [_spirit song_](/Spells.aspx?ID=2029), explicitly damage a creature’s spirit.

You can return to your body as a free action. If you are in spirit form at the beginning of your turn, you must attempt another backlash check for your deviation, returning to your body if you fail.

**Awakening** Your spirit moves at the speed of thought. You gain a [fly Speed](/Rules.aspx?ID=2350) and a +20-foot status bonus to your Speed while in spirit form.

**Awakening** Time seems to pass more slowly while you are projecting your spirit. When you enter spirit form, you can [Recall Knowledge](/Rules.aspx?ID=2638) or [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301). You are [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=89) while in spirit form and can use the extra action only to Recall Knowledge or Seek.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=534" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=389" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 113

**Prerequisites**
[aloof firmament hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=7); [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

**Trigger**
You hit a target with a Spellstrike.

</column>

---

You flow around your foe, using the magic of your attack to carry you away. You [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=2298), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2377), or [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=2378), and this movement doesn’t trigger reactions from the creature you hit. If you High Jump or Long Jump, you don’t have to perform the initial Stride (nor do you fall if you don’t Stride 10 feet). 

The lightness of your steps persists after the jump, granting you the ability to land on or walk on the surface of water or other liquids until the end of your next turn.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 28

**Prerequisites**
[offensive boost](/Classes.aspx?ID=19)

**Trigger**
A creature within your reach uses a [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) action.

</column>

---

Your enemies think they can concentrate on something else while you're nearby? Oh, you'll give them a distraction, all right! Make a melee Strike against the triggering creature with a weapon or [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that is benefiting from your offensive boost. This Strike doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty, and your multiple attack penalty doesn't apply to this Strike.

 **Unstable Function** You pull out all the stops to create an explosive distraction. Add the [unstable](/Traits.aspx?ID=416) trait to Distracting Explosion. If the attack hits, you disrupt the triggering concentrate action.

**Special** If your innovation is a [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109), it can take this reaction instead of you, even though minions can't normally take reactions or act when it's not their turn. It uses your reaction for the turn to do so.

You don't need to be observing your ally or know where they are, but you need to know they're present to choose them.

You weave distracting magic with one hand to enhance your Spellstrike. Make a Spellstrike and [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48) against the target of your Strike.     level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=953" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 19

**Prerequisites**
[laughing shadow hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=11); [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=4260)

**Requirements**
You have a hand free, and your Spellstrike is charged.

</column>

---

You weave distracting magic with one hand to enhance the efficacy of your [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755). Make a Spellstrike and [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390) against the target of your [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306). Execute your Feint immediately before making the Strike, but after choosing your target. The Feint gains the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534) and [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) traits, and it always has the basic effects of a Feint, rather than applying any adjustments or alternate effects from other feats or abilities.

If you're in the [Arcane Cascade](/Actions.aspx?ID=756) stance, you gain a status bonus to your [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) check equal to your extra damage from Arcane Cascade (typically 1, increasing to 2 if you have weapon specialization and 3 if you have greater weapon specialization).

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Bravado" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=801" />
<trait label="Flourish" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=606" />
<trait label="Swashbuckler" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=825" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 167

</column>

---

You toss one weapon into the air as a distraction as you throw another. Choose a creature within 30 feet and [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=2390) against it; you can attempt this Feint even if the target is not within melee range, and if the target becomes [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) as a result of the Feint, this applies to your [thrown](/Traits.aspx?ID=711) weapon attacks for the duration. Regardless of the result, you can then Interact to draw a thrown weapon and make a thrown weapon Strike against the target. If you have an open hand, you then catch the weapon you originally tossed into the air unless you critically failed at your attempt to Feint, in which case it lands on the ground at your feet.

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 281

You are at least 20 feet above the ground. 

</column>

---

You dive from the sky, bringing down the might of the divine with you. You [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=2312) straight down, landing safely in the nearest unoccupied space directly below you. When you land, all creatures in a 10-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) take 8d10 [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=737) damage ([basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC). On a failure, the target is pushed 5 feet (or 10 feet on a critical failure).

At 20th level, the spirit damage increases to 10d10.

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 42

---

Your wandering studies mean you've heard rumors or theories about almost every topic... though admittedly, your sources aren't always the most reliable. You can take a –2 penalty to your check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) with [Esoteric Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) to Recall Knowledge about any topic, not just the usual topics available for Esoteric Lore. Additionally, when you succeed at your check to [Exploit a Vulnerability](/Actions.aspx?ID=1227), compare the result of your Esoteric Lore check to the DC to Recall Knowledge for that creature; if that number would be a success or a critical success, you gain information as if you had succeeded at the Recall Knowledge check.

    right="Feat 16"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Diverse Mystery](/Feats.aspx?ID=1505) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Oracle" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=319" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 81

**Prerequisites**
[Advanced Revelation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1492)

</column>

---

You have broadened your understanding of the divine and can tap into the wonders of a different mystery. Select one revelation spell from a mystery other than your own. You can choose only an initial revelation spell or an advanced revelation spell.

 When you cast this revelation spell, you gain the effects of the minor curse from that mystery in addition to the normal curse effects you gain from casting a revelation spell. This additional minor curse effect remains until your next daily preparations. Any ability that lets you cast a revelation spell without increasing the severity of your curse also prevents you from gaining this additional curse effect.

 You can't cast your chosen revelation spell if any of the following conditions are true: its mystery's curse effects directly conflict with or negate the effects of your own mystery's curse, the curse would have no effect on you (for example, removing an ability from your original mystery that you lack), or either of these criteria would be met once you finish Casting the Spell.

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 86 **Archetype** [Warshard Warrior](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=341) **Prerequisites** [Warshard Warrior Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8178) **Requirements** You are wielding a melee warshard weapon. --- When you face multiple foes, you wield your warshard weapon with vigor. Spend 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323), then Step to a space where you threaten at least two opponents with your warshard weapon. Attempt two Strikes at mythic proficiency, each against a different target. If you hit with both Strikes, you gain an additional effect based on the type of damage you inflict with your weapon. Both attacks count toward your [multiple attack penalty](/Rules.aspx?ID=2289), but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made both of them. If your weapon doesn’t deal one of these three damage types, you can’t use it to Divide and Conquer, and if you deal two different types of damage to each target, you don’t gain any additional effect. • **Bludgeoning** You knock your enemies around. Each damaged target becomes [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of your next turn.
• **Piercing** Your strikes punch through your enemies, leaving bloody wounds. Each damaged target takes 1d8 persistent bleed damage.
• **Slashing** Your slashes leave particularly painful wounds. Each damaged target becomes sickened 2.

fields.text: Feat 16 Divide and Conquer Two Actions Mythic Source Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star pg. 86 Archetype Warshard Warrior Prerequisites Warshard Warrior Dedication Requirements You are wielding a melee warshard weapon. When you face multiple foes, you wield your warshard weapon with vigor. Spend 1 Mythic Point, then Step to a space where you threaten at least two opponents with your warshard weapon. Attempt two Strikes at mythic proficiency, each against a different target. If you hit with both Strikes, you gain an additional effect based on the type of damage you inflict with your weapon. Both attacks count toward your multiple attack penalty, but the penalty doesn’t increase until after you’ve made both of them. If your weapon doesn’t deal one of these three damage types, you can’t use it to Divide and Conquer, and if you deal two different types of damage to each target, you don’t gain any additional effect. • Bludgeoning You knock your enemies around. Each damaged target becomes off-guard until the start of your next turn. • Piercing Your strikes punch through your enemies, leaving bloody wounds. Each damaged target takes 1d8 persistent bleed damage. • Slashing Your slashes leave particularly painful wounds. Each damaged target becomes sickened 2.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Divine Emissary](/Feats.aspx?ID=3633) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Sorcerer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=148" />
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 83

**Prerequisites**
a [familiar](/Familiars.aspx), you follow a good-aligned deity or patron

**Access**
Knights of Lastwall have access to this feat.

</column>

---

Your familiar is a divine emissary, sent to you by your deity or patron and infused with celestial powers. You can select one additional familiar ability each day, which must be one of the following divine emissary familiar abilities. You can't select more than one divine emissary familiar ability at a time.

 **Erudite** Your familiar has incredible religious knowledge. Despite being a minion, your familiar gains 1 reaction at the start of its turns, which it can use only to [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) you on a [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) check (it still has to prepare to help you as normal for the Aid reaction). It automatically succeeds its check to Aid you with Religion checks or automatically critically succeeds if you're a master in Religion.

 **Luminous** Your familiar glows with a comforting light. It sheds bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for the next 30 feet. It can suppress or resume this light by using an action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait.

 **Medic** Your familiar can draw upon the power of your deity to Cast a Spell once per day. The familiar can cast the 1-action version of [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) at a level 2 levels lower than your highest-level spell slot, which it can cast only on you. You must be able to cast 3rd-level spells from spell slots to select this ability.

 **Radiant** Your familiar is filled with a divine radiance that makes it resistant to the forces of evil. Your familiar gains resistance to evil and [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118) damage equal to half your level.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Divine Health](/Feats.aspx?ID=5893) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=811" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 94

</column>

---

Your faith makes you resistant to disease, protecting you as you offer succor to the ill. You gain a +2 status bonus to saves against [diseases](/Traits.aspx?ID=578) and [poisons](/Traits.aspx?ID=669) and to flat checks to recover from [persistent poison damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). Allies in your champion's aura get this benefit, but their bonus is +1.

 In addition, if you roll a success on a save against a disease or poison, you get a critical success instead. (Your allies don't share this benefit.) If you have the sacred body class feature, when you roll a critical failure on a save against a disease or poison, you get a failure instead.

[Divine Infusion](/Feats.aspx?ID=4657) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=554" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 116

</column>

---

You pour energy into the subject of your healing to empower its attacks. If the next action you use is to cast harm or heal to restore Hit Points to a single creature, the target then deals an additional 1d6 damage with its melee weapons and unarmed attacks until the end of its next turn. The damage type is void if you cast harm and vitality if you cast heal.

If the spell cast is at least 5th rank, this damage increases to 2d6, and if the spell is at least 8th rank, the damage increases to 3d6.

Though you are not yet a god, you can invoke a measure of omnipotence that makes you high invulnerable. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320). </traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 281

**Archetype** [Mortal Herald](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=305)

**Prerequisites**
[Mortal Herald Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7528)

</column>

---

Your spirit becomes one with your deity, granting you the bearing of a god. As long as you are in this stance, you have a 5-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) that has the [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=542) trait. Whenever you take an action, you can take it from your space or any space within the emanation as if it were the space you occupy. An enemy that ends its turn completely within the emanation is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to your Strikes. You can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) the emanation to increase its radius by 5 feet, up to a maximum of 15 feet.

</traits>

You’re practiced in using your fans to spin with dizzying speed. [Tumble Through](/Actions.aspx?ID=2370) an opponent’s space, and then [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) that opponent. If this second Tumble Through and Strike are successful, you can repeat these actions a third time against a third opponent.

feat: Do You Know Who I Am?
fields.feat_markdown: Do You Know Who I Am?
fields.markdown:
**Source** [Hellfire Dispatches](/Sources.aspx?ID=319) pg. 47 **Archetype** [Dandy](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=246) **Prerequisites** [Dandy Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=6302); Master in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) --- Your reputation casts a long shadow, allowing you to throw your cultural weight around, especially in larger settlements. With a well-timed tirade or attention-getting shout, you can break a foe's mind and bring them low. Choose a foe within 30 feet, and attempt an Intimidation check against the target's Will DC. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to this check if you're in a city or a +2 circumstance bonus to this check if you're in a metropolis. If you're specifically in Absalom, the bonus is instead +3. The target is then temporarily immune to your Do You Know Who I Am? for 24 hours. **Critical Success** The target takes 12d6 mental damage and becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 3. It can't reduce its frightened condition below 1 if it ends its turn adjacent to you.
**Success** The target takes 6d6 mental damage and becomes frightened 2.
**Failure** The target is unaffected.
**Critical Failure** The target is unaffected, and the embarrassment causes you to take 6d6 mental damage.

You use your acrobatic prowess to evade an attack, using momentum to keep yourself moving, if you choose. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack. </title>

<traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 279

**Archetype** [Mortal Herald](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=305)

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

Your deity contains multitudes, and you can express any aspect of them you desire. During your daily preparations, you can gain two initial or advanced domain spells from any of your deity’s domains or alternate domains. You can cast these as innate spells until your next daily preparations. 

Domain spells are a type of focus spell. Casting any of your [focus](/Rules.aspx?ID=285) spells costs you 1 Focus Point. The maximum number of Focus Points in your pool is equal to the number of focus spells you know or 3, whichever is lower. You refill your focus pool during your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), and you can regain 1 Focus Point by spending 10 minutes using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=2621) activity to pray to your deity or do service toward their causes. Your domain spells are [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spells. If you were not already, you become trained in spell attacks and spell DCs. Your spellcasting attribute for domain spells is Wisdom.

Your deity bestows a special spell related to their powers. Select one domain—a subject of particular interest to you within your religion—from your deity's list. You gain an initial domain spell for that domain, a spell unique to the domain and not available to other clerics. Each domain's theme and domain spells can be found [here](/Domains.aspx).

 Domain spells are a type of focus spell. It costs 1 Focus Point to cast a focus spell, and you start with a focus pool of 1 Focus Point. You refill your focus pool during your daily preparations, and you can regain 1 Focus Point by spending 10 minutes using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity to pray to your deity or do service toward their causes.

 Focus spells are automatically heightened to half your level rounded up. Focus spells don't require spell slots, nor can you cast them using spell slots. Certain feats can give you more focus spells and increase the size of your focus pool, though your focus pool can never hold more than 3 Focus Points. The full rules for focus spells appear [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=276).

**Special** You can select this feat multiple times, selecting a different domain each time and gaining its domain spell.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 6"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Domain Spirit](/Feats.aspx?ID=7573) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Exploration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=66" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 292

**Archetype** [Rivethun Emissary](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=308)

**Prerequisites**
[Rivethun Emissary Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7571)

</column>

---

You forge an intense spiritual bond of mutual trust and appreciation with a single spirit that you have already bonded with using Bond with Spirit. Forming this bond takes 24 hours of communion, during which time you must remain within 30 feet of the creature or within that terrain. If the creature is intelligent, this also requires that creature’s consent, and that intelligent creature can choose to sever this bond with you at any time as a free action, which has the concentrate trait. This spirit is your domain spirit. The bond between you and your domain spirit is not weakened by time or distance, but you can only maintain one such bond at a time, regardless of how many bonded spirits you can maintain.

Select one domain related to your domain spirit. You always have the option to select the [healing](/Domains.aspx?ID=78) or [soul](/Domains.aspx?ID=51) domain. If your spirit is a creature, select your domain from the following: [ambition](/Domains.aspx?ID=64), [confidence](/Domains.aspx?ID=67), [family](/Domains.aspx?ID=74), [might](/Domains.aspx?ID=83), [protection](/Domains.aspx?ID=90), or [trickery](/Domains.aspx?ID=94). If your spirit is a terrain, select your domain from the following: [air](/Domains.aspx?ID=65), [cities](/Domains.aspx?ID=66), [darkness](/Domains.aspx?ID=69), [earth](/Domains.aspx?ID=73), [nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=85), [travel](/Domains.aspx?ID=93), [water](/Domains.aspx?ID=98), or [wood](/Domains.aspx?ID=63). If your spirit has a trait that shares a name with a domain, you can add that domain to your list of available options. Your GM can choose to add domains to your list of available options, to represent your domain spirit’s unique interests. The domain you select from among your available options must have a clear connection to your domain spirit. For example, if you bond with a [fire elemental](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=410), you add the [fire](/Domains.aspx?ID=76) domain to the list of options available to you, but if you bond with a deserted tropical island, you can’t select the cities domain, even though it’s among the options usually available to terrain spirits. Your GM is the final arbiter of which domains you can select from. You gain the initial domain spell for that domain. This domain spell is a Rivethun focus spell.

You can choose to bond with a new domain spirit, ending your bond with your current domain spirit and bonding with a different one, to change your selected domain. This process takes 24 hours and follows all the same requirements for forming a bond with your initial domain spirit. During this time of communion, you do not have access to your domain spells granted by your domain spirit. When this bond is formed with your new domain spirit, select one domain related to your new spirit, following the above rules for selecting a domain.

The bond between you and your domain spirit is not weakened by time or distance, but you can only maintain one such bond at a time, regardless of how many bonded spirits you can maintain. Select one domain related to your domain spirit. You always have the option to select the healing or soul domain. If your spirit is a creature, select your domain from the following: ambition, confidence, family, might, protection, or trickery. If your spirit is a terrain, select your domain from the following: air, cities, darkness, earth, nature, travel, water, or wood. If your spirit has a trait that shares a name with a domain, you can add that domain to your list of available options. Your GM can choose to add domains to your list of available options, to represent your domain spirit’s unique interests. The domain you select from among your available options must have a clear connection to your domain spirit. For example, if you bond with a fire elemental, you add the fire domain to the list of options available to you, but if you bond with a deserted tropical island, you can’t select the cities domain, even though it’s among the options usually available to terrain spirits. Your GM is the final arbiter of which domains you can select from. You gain the initial domain spell for that domain. This domain spell is a Rivethun focus spell. You can choose to bond with a new domain spirit, ending your bond with your current domain spirit and bonding with a different one, to change your selected domain. This process takes 24 hours and follows all the same requirements for forming a bond with your initial domain spirit. During this time of communion, you do not have access to your domain spells granted by your domain spirit. When this bond is formed with your new domain spirit, select one domain related to your new spirit, following the above rules for selecting a domain. Domain Spirit leads to... Advanced Domain Spirit

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Vampire](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=181)

**Prerequisites**
[Manipulative Charm](/Feats.aspx?ID=3547)

</column>

---

You stare into your target's eyes and enthrall them, shattering their free will. Once per day, you can cast 7th-level [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=87) as a divine innate spell, using your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. It gains the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) trait. At 18th level, the dominate is heightened to 8th level; at 20th level, it's heightened to 9th level. A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune to your domination for 24 hours, though in most cases, you can't Cast the Spell again within 24 hours. If you are destroyed, all your _dominate_ spells from Dominating Gaze immediately end.

For a short time, you fully manifest the expectations of the god destroyer within you. fields.text: Feat 14 Dormant Eruption Rare Aftermath Fire Primal Source Dark Archive (Remastered) pg. 57 Prerequisites You've been brought to 0 Hit Points by an enemy that has the fire trait or an enemy's ability that has the fire trait. A sweltering heat and sparks of flame that take the form of tiny copies of you surround your body. You're hot to the touch, gaining resistance 5 to cold and fire. Whenever an adjacent creature Strikes you with a melee attack or touches you, it takes 1d6 persistent fire damage. You gain the Thermal Eruption action. Thermal Eruption Two Actions (fire, primal) Frequency once per day; Effect You concentrate your thermal energy and explode it outward. All creatures in a 20-foot emanation take 14d6 fire damage with a basic Reflex save. Afterward, you lose all effects of the Dormant Eruption feat until your next daily preparations.
