<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #164: Hands of the Devil](/Sources.aspx?ID=75) pg. 76

**Archetype** [Eldritch Researcher](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=89)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2); Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11)

</column>

---

You gain the ability to cast a single arcane or occult cantrip of your choice (which is heightened to a spell level equal to half your level rounded up). If you weren't already, you become trained in that tradition's spell DCs and spell attack rolls with Intelligence as your spellcasting ability.

 Regardless of whether you choose an arcane or occult cantrip, you also become an expert in your choice of either Arcana or Occultism. You also gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks you attempt with the chosen skill when [Investigating](/Actions.aspx?ID=516) or [Identifying Magic](/Actions.aspx?ID=24).

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the Eldritch Researcher archetype.

<title level="2">Eldritch Researcher Dedication leads to...</title>
[Able Ritualist](/Feats.aspx?ID=2662), [Advanced Seeker of Truths](/Feats.aspx?ID=2665), [Entities from Afar](/Feats.aspx?ID=2667), [Incredible Recollection](/Feats.aspx?ID=2668), [Know it All](/Feats.aspx?ID=2664), [Lorefinder](/Feats.aspx?ID=2663), [Scholarly Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=2661), [Seeker of Truths](/Feats.aspx?ID=2659), [Strange Script](/Feats.aspx?ID=2660), [Words of Unraveling](/Feats.aspx?ID=2666)

</column>

---

You electrify your armor to punish foes who dare to attack you. For 1 round, any creature that touches you, or that hits you with a melee [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack or a non-[reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=192) melee weapon attack, takes 1d4 electricity damage. The effect ends if you cease wearing your armor innovation.

 If you have the revolutionary innovation class feature, the damage increases to 2d4.

 **Unstable Function** You create an unstable chain reaction, sending countless sparks dancing across your armor. Add the [unstable](/Traits.aspx?ID=416) trait to Electrify Armor. The effects last for 1 minute instead of 1 round, and the damage dice increase from d4s to d12s.

<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 36

</column>

---

Spinning wood and metal together, you create a rugged wooden ballista. The ballista is Medium and appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet. It immediately shoots a bolt with a jagged tip of elemental metal. Make an impulse attack roll against the AC of a target within 120 feet. The target takes 3d12 piercing damage on a hit (or double damage on a critical hit).

 The ballista can be shot again, but it must first be reloaded with two Interact actions. The ballista lasts until the end of your next turn, and you can Sustain the impulse. Each time you Sustain it, you can roll the ballista up to 20 feet, shoot it if it's loaded, or contribute 1 action toward reloading it.

---
**Level (+3)** The damage increases by 1d12.

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 206 **Archetype** [Elementalist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=98) **Prerequisites** [Elementalist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2986); [Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=604) --- Your familiar becomes an elemental spirit capable of taking on aspects of the four elements: air, earth, fire, or water. Other than taking the form of an [elemental](/Traits.aspx?ID=57) instead of an animal, this familiar continues to use all the same rules as other familiars. Your familiar gains one additional familiar ability each day, which must be one of the following elemental familiar abilities. While your familiar has an elemental familiar ability, your familiar is composed of the associated elemental matter and gains the matching elemental trait. You can't select more than one elemental familiar ability at a time.
  • **Air** If your familiar stays completely still for 1 round, it becomes [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) until it next takes an action. Any motion, even being moved or carried by another creature, ends this effect.
  • **Earth** Your familiar gains resistance to physical damage (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374)) equal to half your level.
  • **Fire** Your familiar sheds bright light in a 20-foot radius (and dim light for the next 20 feet) and emits warmth. Creatures that remain within a 15-foot emanation don't take damage from [severe environmental cold](/Rules.aspx?ID=642).
  • **Water** Your familiar can move through a gap at least 2 inches wide without [Squeezing](/Actions.aspx?ID=31) and can Squeeze through a gap at least 1 inch wide.

A small creature made of elemental matter springs forth from your kinetic gate. This elemental [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=160) appears to be made of one of your kinetic elements, though it might have unusual or distinguishing aspects. Like other familiars, your elemental familiar can assist you in various tasks and on adventures. You gain an [elemental familiar](/Familiars.aspx?ID=93) with the trait of one of your kinetic elements. If you have more than one kinetic element, you can change the element you've selected for your familiar to a different one of your kinetic elements each time you make your daily preparations. The familiar uses your Constitution modifier to determine its Perception, [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1), and [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) modifiers.

---

You can scratch out and rewrite part of an elemental rune to temporarily change the type of power it channels. You touch an adjacent [_corrosive_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2834), [_flaming_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2838), [_frost_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2839), [_shock_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2847), or [_thundering_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2850) rune on an unattended item or one held or worn by a willing creature, and you change it to any other rune from that list. You can also revise the greater version of any of the above runes into the greater version of any other rune on the list (for instance, _greater corrosive_ into _greater frost_). The revision lasts for 1 minute before the rune’s original magic reasserts itself.

---

Your elven blood runs particularly strong, granting you features far more elven than those of a typical aiuvarin. You may also have been raised among elves, steeped in your elven ancestors’ heritage. You gain the benefits of the elf heritage of your elven parent or ancestors. You typically can’t select a heritage that depends on or improves an elven feature you don’t have. For example, you couldn’t take the [Ancient Elf](/Heritages.aspx?ID=34) heritage unless your non-elf ancestry also has a lifespan measured in multiple centuries. In these cases, at the GM’s discretion, you might gain a different benefit.

**Special** You can take this feat only at 1st level, and you can’t retrain out of this feat or into this feat.

[Elven Aloofness](/Feats.aspx?ID=1408) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 43

---

As much as you might care for them, you've come to terms with the ephemeral nature of non-elves, and it makes their threats feel less troublesome. If a non-elf rolls a failure on a check to [Coerce](/Actions.aspx?ID=52) you using [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7), it gets a critical failure instead (and thus can't try to Coerce you again for 1 week). When a non-elf attempts to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) you, you become temporarily immune for 1 day, instead of 10 minutes.

<column gap="tiny">

---

Athamarus have bonded with eels more closely than any other fish. You have formed a strong connection with a young eel that serves as your pet. Typically, these eels are tended until they grow large enough to serve as a mount. You gain the [Pet](/Feats.aspx?ID=5186) general feat. Instead of the normal choice of pet abilities, your eel has aquatic, [fast movement](/Familiars.aspx?ID=144), and the [damage avoidance](/Familiars.aspx?ID=110) familiar ability for Reflex saves. The aquatic ability means it gains the [aquatic](/Traits.aspx?ID=533) trait, breathes water instead of air, and has a swim Speed instead of a land Speed.

 When you aren't in an aquatic environment, you can easily carry your pet eel around in a small water-filled globe that has light Bulk.

[Emancipator's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3434) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Strength of Thousands</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

**Archetypes** [Druid](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=6), [Wizard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=12) (Level 20), [Wizard](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=218) (Level 20)

**Prerequisites**
[Druid Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=701) or [Wizard Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=742)

</column>

---

Your mask grants you the abilities of Whistling Kite, the Vigilant Seer, who emancipated thousands. When you are attempting a check to free someone else from an effect that [immobilizes](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24), [paralyzes](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), or [controls](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6) them, roll twice and take the higher result; this is a [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76) effect. The GM might decide that this fortune effect applies when attempting checks to remove other conditions or effects to free another. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only one creature, you can choose to permit the target to make an attempt to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79).

<title level="2">Masks of the Magic Warriors</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

In becoming Jatembe's new Magic Warriors, the heroes have unlocked secrets of magical potential that none have reached since the earliest Ten Magic Warriors walked the plazas of the Magaambya.

 On reaching 20th level, the heroes should have the option of taking one of these archetype feats, based on the type of animal they chose for their mask when they first created it in _Pathfinder Adventure Path #169: Kindled Magic_. These options are each themed to one of Jatembe's magic warriors, but if a hero's mask doesn't fit with a specific animal from this list or the player feels their animal embodies a different effect from the list, feel free to reflavor the feat names to fit the hero's spirit face. For instance, the Cunning Trickster mask could easily be a rodent or a fox, not just a spider.

**Related Feats**: [Cunning Trickster Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3433), [Grand Medic's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3435), [Protective Spirit Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3436), [Sky Master Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3437), [Stalking Feline Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3438), [Storyteller's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3439), [Thick Hide Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3440), [Tireless Guide's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3441), [Vigilant Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3442)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Downtime" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=49" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 240

**Archetype** [Runelord](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=103)

**Prerequisites**
[Runelord Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3020); Trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4)

</column>

---

You discover the secrets to embedding [_aeon stones_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=407) into your flesh. You spend 1 day attuning to an _aeon stone_ and physically embedding it in your skin. While the stone is embedded this way, you gain the benefits of the _aeon stone_ as if it were orbiting above your head, but it protects the stone from being noticed or stolen as easily. _Aeon stones_ in your flesh must be invested to function, as usual.

 You can also use this activity to safely remove an embedded _aeon stone_ in 1 day. Someone without this feat can attempt to surgically remove it safely by spending 1 day and succeeding at a DC 30 [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9) check, or hastily by simply ripping it from a corpse.

<title level="2">Embed Aeon Stone leads to...</title>
[Aeon Resonance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3022)

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 122 --- Carefully etching a sacred image into a physical object, you steel yourself for battle. You can spend 10 minutes emblazoning a symbol of your deity upon a weapon or shield. The symbol doesn’t fade until 1 year has passed, but if you Emblazon an Armament, any symbol you previously emblazoned and any symbol already emblazoned on that item instantly disappears. fields.text: Feat 2 Emblazon Armament Cleric Exploration Source Player Core pg. 115 Carefully etching a sacred image into a physical object, you steel yourself for battle. You can spend 10 minutes emblazoning a symbol of your deity upon a weapon or shield. The symbol doesn’t fade until 1 year has passed, but if you Emblazon an Armament, any symbol you previously emblazoned, and any symbol already emblazoned on that item instantly disappears. The emblazoned item is a religious symbol of your deity in addition to its normal purpose, and it gains another benefit determined by the type of item. The benefit applies only to followers of the deity the symbol represents, but others can use the item normally. Shield The shield gains a +1 status bonus to its Hardness. (This causes it to reduce more damage with the Shield Block reaction.). Weapon The wielder gains a +1 status bonus to damage rolls with the weapon. Emblazon Armament leads to... Emblazon Antimagic, Emblazon Energy

>
[Emblazon Divinity](/Feats.aspx?ID=1164) <actions string="" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Age of Ashes</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Cleric" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=26" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 76

**Prerequisites**
[Emblazon Armament](/Feats.aspx?ID=272)

</column>

---

Your sacred etchings imbue objects with power. It takes you only 1 minute to emblazon a symbol using [Emblazon Armament](/Feats.aspx?ID=272), and you can have up to four symbols emblazoned at a time. Each item can still have only one symbol emblazoned upon it, and if you exceed the limit of four, the oldest symbol disappears. These symbols can benefit even those who don’t follow the deity, provided they aren’t directly opposed (as determined by the GM).

 You can select a different benefit for each emblazoned symbol, chosen from any you have from Emblazon Armament or other feats such as [Emblazon Energy](/Feats.aspx?ID=289) or [Emblazon Antimagic](/Feats.aspx?ID=296).

<title level="2">Paragons of Promise</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 75

The citizens of Promise represent some of the most capable experts, greatest minds, and powerful warriors on Golarion—ideal teachers and trainers for PCs who want to maximize their own potential. If the PCs secure Visitor’s Pins or an alliance with Mengkare, their access to Promise’s trainers and records unlock all of the following uncommon class feats.

**Related Feats**: [Apex Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1160), [Aura of Unbreakable Virtue](/Feats.aspx?ID=1161), [Bloodline Metamorphosis](/Feats.aspx?ID=1162), [Efficient Alchemy (Paragon)](/Feats.aspx?ID=1163), [Enduring Debilitation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1165), [Golden Body](/Feats.aspx?ID=1166), [Song of the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=1168), [Spell Mastery](/Feats.aspx?ID=1843), [Superior Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=1170), [Ultimate Flexibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=1732), [Unstoppable Juggernaut](/Feats.aspx?ID=1631)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Embodied Dragoon Subjectivity](/Feats.aspx?ID=3929) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fleshwarp" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=338" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 29

</column>

---

When your allies call for swift reinforcements or lightning raids, you're ready to answer. Your titanic form encompasses both cavalry and rider so that you're able to traverse vast distances and exploit opportunities in the theater of war. Your pores distend and extrude copious amounts of blood, subcutaneous fat, and lymphatic fluid for you to harden and flash-sculpt into gliding wings or a swift-hurtling mount. You can cast [_feather fall_](/Spells.aspx?ID=111) and [_phantom steed_](/Spells.aspx?ID=221) each once per day as innate occult spells. When you cast _feather fall_ in this way, gliding wings slow your fall, and when you cast _phantom steed_ in this way, the steed physically protrudes from your own lower body. Neither of these cosmetic changes alter the spells' effects; for example, foes can still attack the _phantom steed_ as normal.

</column>

---

Your colossal might marks you as a behemoth, the pride of Nex's Fleshforges, and the heaviest ordnance is a child's toy in your monumental grasp. You're a dreadnought, a living siege weapon, albeit one that wields other siege weapons in battle as your endoskeleton and flesh toughens. You gain the [Hefty Hauler](/Feats.aspx?ID=790) skill feat, and your maximum Bulk limit further increases by 3, for a total of 2 to your [encumbered](/Conditions.aspx?ID=12) limit and 5 to your maximum limit.

Nex's Fleshforges shaped you not to achieve individual greatness at arms, but rather to become a part of a legion, a modular piece integral to the combined arms stratagems of Nexian battlemages. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 102

**Archetype** [Magaambyan Attendant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=29)

**Prerequisites**
[Magaambyan Attendant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1102); Expert in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14); Emerald Boughs affiliation

</column>

---

You are comfortable and socially capable in almost any cultural context. When you use the Society skill to [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=27), if you roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead; if you roll a success, you get a critical success instead; and if you roll a critical success, you can provide for another additional creature. Furthermore, when you attempt a Society check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) about cultural practices and roll a critical failure, you get a failure instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Emerald Boughs Hideaway](/Feats.aspx?ID=1111) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 103

**Archetype** [Magaambyan Attendant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=29)

**Prerequisites**
[Magaambyan Attendant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1102); Emerald Boughs affiliation

</column>

---

You use Emerald Bough techniques to create a small extradimensional space called a hideaway that lasts as long as you are conscious. The hideaway functions as a [_type I bag of holding_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=249), but has no Bulk and takes no hands; it holds one object with a maximum Bulk equal to your highest mental ability score modifier; as you open the hideaway with pure thought, activating it to retrieve an item is a free action with the envision component instead of a single action with the Interact component. The hideaway’s access point appears as an obviously magical gap within 1 foot of your body. Only you can access the hideaway; you can you use an Interact action each round to physically hold it open for another person. A successful [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) spell or similar effect against your spell DC and the hideaway’s counteract level of 2 expels the object; the object is also expelled if you become unconscious. After a successful _dispel magic _spell or when you become conscious again, the hideaway immediately reforms with no additional action from you. You can also dismiss the hideaway (if it is empty) or re-form it using a single action with the envision component.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 52

**Archetype** [Swordmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=33)

**Prerequisites**
[Swordmaster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1139); Master in [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9)

**Requirements**
An adjacent ally is suffering [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).

</column>

---

You've learned a variety of methods for helping allies who are bleeding, burning, or otherwise suffering persistent damage, from brushing off acid to patting down fires. Your ally immediately attempts a flat check to remove all types of persistent damage, and your use of this feat automatically counts as especially effective aid, reducing the DC from 15 to 10 for all future flat checks to remove the persistent damage.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Emissary Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=7572) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=535" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 292

**Archetype** [Rivethun Emissary](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=308)

**Prerequisites**
[Rivethun Emissary Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7571)

</column>

---

You forge a mystical bond with a spirit or create a spirit from a fragment of your own soul. You gain a familiar. If you already have a familiar, you gain the [Enhanced Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=4717) feat.

Your familiar gains two additional [familiar abilities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2125) each day, one of which must be used to select the following master ability.

**Synchronize Spirit** You can synchronize your spiritual energy with that of your familiar to temporarily become part spirit yourself. Once per round, you can [Sustain](/Actions.aspx?ID=2317) to synchronize your spirit with that of your familiar. You remain synchronized with your spirit until the beginning of your next turn. While synchronized, whenever you [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) or [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) without a duration that deals damage, you deal spirit damage instead of your normal damage.

>
[Emissary of Peace](/Feats.aspx?ID=3580) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 74

**Archetype** [Knight Vigilant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=27)

**Prerequisites**
[Knight Vigilant](/Feats.aspx?ID=1092); Master in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6)

</column>

---

Even when bloodshed is inevitable, you would rather see your foes surrender. You attempt a Diplomacy check to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) against a single foe whose Hit Points are at less than half of their maximum value, followed by an immediate [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) to convince that creature to cease fighting. You take a –5 penalty to your Diplomacy check. The GM sets the DC of the Request based on the circumstances; it's generally at least a very hard DC for the creature's level. Some creatures might simply refuse, and those who agree to parley might find your arguments lacking and start fighting again.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #189: Dreamers of the Nameless Spires](/Sources.aspx?ID=195) pg. 78

**Archetype** [Twilight Speaker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=203)

**Prerequisites**
[Twilight Speaker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=4114)

</column>

---

You believe that treating others with respect is the fastest way into their hearts, and in turn others are more likely to believe in your good intentions and write off bad first impressions as flukes. If a creature's attitude towards you becomes lower over the course of a social interaction (for example, from [friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=18) to [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=25), or from indifferent to [unfriendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=40)), their impression of you returns to its starting level an hour after the social interaction ends. This ability has no effect if the creature you are interacting with becomes [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23).

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 44 **Prerequisites** Trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) **Trigger** You are attacked by a creature that you haven't yet acted hostile toward. You must use this reaction before the creature rolls its attack. --- The way you cringe or use those puppydog eyes you've been practicing elicits an empathetic response in the attacker. Attempt a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) check against your attacker's Will DC. **Critical Success** The creature pulls its attack, wasting its action, and can't use hostile actions against you until the beginning of its next turn.
**Success** The creature takes a –2 circumstance penalty to damage on the triggering Strike and all its Strikes against you until the beginning of its next turn. The penalty is –4 if you're an expert in Diplomacy, –6 if you're a master, and –8 if you're legendary.
**Failure** The creature's attack is unaffected, and the creature is temporarily immune to your Empathic Pleas for 24 hours.

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<trait label="Reincarnated" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=783" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #199: To Bloom Below the Web](/Sources.aspx?ID=225) pg. 79

</column>

---

Reincarnation has given you a compassionate perspective and enabled you to relate to almost everyone you speak with, putting them at ease and quickly generating trust. Whenever you attempt a Diplomacy check to [Make An Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) or [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) something, the DC is reduced by 2, and if the creature you're speaking with is lower level than you, any success is a critical success. Whenever you attempt a Diplomacy check to [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=2391), you can't critically fail.

Sharp and piercing, your eyes see all and convey more. Your [Point Out](/Actions.aspx?ID=2315) actions lose the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=541) trait, and you don't need to be heard to convey the information to your allies. In addition, a creature you Point Out is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) to your allies until the start of your next turn.

**Special** If you have the [Blind-Fight](/Feats.aspx?ID=4809) feat, your allies gain that feat's benefits against any creature that's off-guard due to Empiricist's Eye.

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 176 **Archetype** [Herbalist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=62) **Prerequisites** [Herbalist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1982); Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) --- During your daily preparations, you find medicinal plants endemic to your location. Until your next preparations, you can spend an additional batch of herbs to add a benefit to an item you create with your herbalism. The benefit of the special herbs affects the creature that the item is applied to; if the benefit is not immediate, it lasts for 1 minute unless otherwise stated. This adjustment counts as an [additive](/Traits.aspx?ID=4), so you can't include another additive without spoiling the item.
  • **Aquatic** Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves.
  • **Arctic** For 1 hour, treat [environmental cold effects](/Rules.aspx?ID=642) as if they were one step less severe.
  • **Desert** For 1 hour, treat environmental heat effects as if they were one step less severe.
  • **Forest** Gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46) and [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126) effects.
  • **Mountain** Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Reflex saves.
  • **Plains** Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves.
  • **Swamp** Remove one source of [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).
  • **Underground** Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception.

Archetype Herbalist Prerequisites Herbalist Dedication; Trained in Survival The herbal items you create use medicinal plants endemic to your location. When a creature consumes one of your herbal items, that creature gains the benefit matching the location where you created that item. If the benefit is not immediate, it lasts for 1 minute unless otherwise stated. Aquatic Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Fortitude saves. Arctic For 1 hour, treat environmental cold effects as if they were one step less severe. Desert For 1 hour, treat environmental heat effects as if they were one step less severe. Forest Gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saves against disease and poison effects. Mountain Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Reflex saves. Plains Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves. Swamp Remove one source of persistent bleed damage. Underground Gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception.

[Endless Memories](/Feats.aspx?ID=3953) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Ghoran" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=352" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 38

**Prerequisites**
[Ancient Memories](/Feats.aspx?ID=3944)

</column>

---

You've lived a thousand lives and done a hundred-thousand things. When you choose a skill in which to become trained with Ancient Memories, you can also choose a skill in which you're already trained and become an expert in that skill. This lasts until your Ancient Memories expires. When the effects of Ancient Memories and Endless Memories expire, you can retrain one of your skill increases. The skill increase you gain from this retraining must either make you trained in the skill you chose with Ancient Memories or make you an expert in the skill you chose with Endless Memories.

<title level="2">Endless Memories leads to...</title>
[Eternal Memories](/Feats.aspx?ID=3957)

</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 72

---

Just as the Vale of Aroden retains light and life despite inhospitable surroundings, you can sustain yourself regardless of your environment. You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe. In addition, you can cast the [_wholeness of body_](/Spells.aspx?ID=488) ki spell almost effortlessly. You can cast it as a free action that triggers at the start of your turn.

    right="Feat 10"

>
[Endure Death's Touch](/Feats.aspx?ID=1094) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 94

**Archetype** [Knight Vigilant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=27)

**Prerequisites**
[Knight Vigilant](/Feats.aspx?ID=1092); expert in medium or heavy armor

**Trigger**
An undead hits you with an unarmed attack.

**Requirements**
You are wearing medium or heavy armor in which you have expert proficiency.

</column>

---

Your conviction redirects the undead’s attack through your armor and then harmlessly away. You gain resistance 5 to physical damage and resistance 10 to negative damage against the triggering attack. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus on any saving throws against effects from the undead’s natural attack; if you succeed at the saving throw, you get a critical success instead.

**Frequency**
once per minute

**Prerequisites**
[Debilitating Strike](/Classes.aspx?ID=10)

**Trigger**
You apply a debilitation to a creature.

</column>

---

You can make your debilitation last an exceptionally long time. The triggering debilitation lasts for 1 minute instead of until the end of your next turn.

<title level="2">Paragons of Promise</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #150: Broken Promises](/Sources.aspx?ID=15) pg. 75

The citizens of Promise represent some of the most capable experts, greatest minds, and powerful warriors on Golarion—ideal teachers and trainers for PCs who want to maximize their own potential. If the PCs secure Visitor’s Pins or an alliance with Mengkare, their access to Promise’s trainers and records unlock all of the following uncommon class feats.

**Related Feats**: [Apex Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=1160), [Aura of Unbreakable Virtue](/Feats.aspx?ID=1161), [Bloodline Metamorphosis](/Feats.aspx?ID=1162), [Efficient Alchemy (Paragon)](/Feats.aspx?ID=1163), [Emblazon Divinity](/Feats.aspx?ID=1164), [Golden Body](/Feats.aspx?ID=1166), [Song of the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=1168), [Spell Mastery](/Feats.aspx?ID=1843), [Superior Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=1170), [Ultimate Flexibility](/Feats.aspx?ID=1732), [Unstoppable Juggernaut](/Feats.aspx?ID=1631)

>

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=615" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=695" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 108

**Prerequisites**
[Prepare Elemental Medicine](/Feats.aspx?ID=7065); Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)

**Access**
Minkai or Forest of Spirits origin

</column>

---

You learn Minkaian traditions about the void and know how to manipulate the five elements to fortify vitality and void energies in the body. When you Prepare Elemental Medicine, you can choose to use [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) instead of the usual skills. If you do, the medicine also grants the recipient [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) 2 and [weakness](/Rules.aspx?ID=2317) 2 based on the element you chose. A wood, earth, or water elemental medicine grants resistance to [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage and weakness to [vitality](/Traits.aspx?ID=509) damage, and a living recipient loses its [immunity](/Rules.aspx?ID=2313) to vitality damage for the duration. A fire or metal elemental medicine grants resistance to vitality damage and weakness to void damage, and an undead recipient loses its immunity to void damage for the duration.

If you’re a master in Occultism, increase the resistance and weakness to 4. If you’re legendary, instead increase them to 8.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Enforce Oath](/Feats.aspx?ID=1684) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 120

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
You've sworn to an [oath](/Traits.aspx?ID=119) against a specific type of creature.

</column>

---

You call on your oath to embolden you in combat. When you Enforce your Oath, select one creature you can see that you've sworn to defeat as part of your oath. You gain a +1 status bonus to AC and saves against attacks and effects by the chosen creature. You also gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls against the chosen creature. However, your dedication to Enforcing your Oath draws your focus away from all other foes. While you are Enforcing your Oath, you take a –1 status penalty to AC, attack rolls, and saves against all other creatures until you stop Enforcing your Oath. 

You stop Enforcing your Oath once the chosen creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points or offers a legitimate surrender to you or your allies. You immediately stop Enforcing your Oath if you are unconscious or if the chosen creature goes [unnoticed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=41) by you for more than 1 minute. You can also stop Enforcing your Oath at any time during your turn as a free action.

---

Your construct unleashes a broad swath of devastation by separating its limbs, deploying hidden armaments, or using a similar technique to wreak havoc. You Command your innovation. Instead of its normal actions, it Strides once, then makes a Strike against each foe within 30 feet of it with a +2 circumstance bonus to its attack rolls. The multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after the construct makes all the attacks.

<trait label="Runesmith" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=952" />

---

After quickly drawing a rune on your weapon, you can transfer the rune to a foe as you knock them down, push them away, or disarm their weapon. Attempt to [Disarm](/Actions.aspx?ID=2383), [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=2380), or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=2382) a target; your weapon must have the corresponding trait. If your skill check is successful, you [Trace a Rune](/Actions.aspx?ID=4264) onto the target of the [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=1167) even if the target is pushed out of range.

You attune your senses to the magical frequencies generated by an allied spellcaster, allowing you to amplify or modify their spells to suit the needs of the moment. Select one willing ally within 30 feet that you can see and choose one of the following spellshape feats: [Conceal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4997), [Nonlethal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=5027), [Reach Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4577), or [Widen Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=4715). The target gains the benefits of the feat on their next turn as though they had taken the [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513) action themselves; this requires them to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) as their first action on their turn.

You disguise the _soul cage_ as any non-magical object of the  same Bulk, and it gains the effects of the [_magic aura_](/Spells.aspx?ID=178) and [_nondetection_](/Spells.aspx?ID=209) spells. The effects have unlimited durations, are heightened to half your level rounded up, and use your spell DC against any attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) them. The magic aura makes your _soul cage_ appear non-magical. You can ignore the effects of any of these spells when dealing with your own _soul cage_. You are mentally alerted whenever your _soul cage_ is damaged.

</column>

---

You are granted access to your deity’s realm and can travel there quickly. You can cast [_interplanar teleport_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1576) once per day as an innate [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2) spell with a casting time of only 1 minute. You act as the planar key for the destination, and you can only travel to your deity’s realm. You and the other targets of the spell always appear in the center of your deity’s realm, and you (but not necessarily your allies) are immune to all the realm’s harmful conditions (such as toxic air or [extreme temperatures](/Rules.aspx?ID=2820)) while there. You can return to your previous location by spending 1 minute picturing your destination; you can bring up to 8 willing creatures back with you in this way, and they need not be the same targets of the previous casting of _interplanar teleport_.

    pfs="Limited"

[Entities from Afar](/Feats.aspx?ID=2667) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #164: Hands of the Devil](/Sources.aspx?ID=75) pg. 76

**Archetype** [Eldritch Researcher](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=89)

**Prerequisites**
[Eldritch Researcher Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2658)

</column>

---

You can call in aberrations to fight for you or to answer questions. You can cast [_summon entity_](/Spells.aspx?ID=321) as an innate occult spell once per day. If you couldn't already cast occult spells, these spells use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability, and you become trained in spell attack rolls and spell DCs for occult spells; if you could already cast occult spells, your proficiency in spell attack rolls and spell DCs for occult spells increases to expert.

 As soon as the [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1) arrives, instead of giving it any other commands, you can demand that it help you with a single question you pose to it. For the creature to effectively answer, you must Sustain the Spell for 1 minute, and you must understand and be understood by the aberration. If you do, the aberration gives you a cryptic clue as provided by the [_read omens_](/Spells.aspx?ID=247) spell, except that the clue is even more enigmatic than normal; the creature then immediately returns from whence it came without providing you any other benefit. At 16th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the _summon entity_ spell is heightened by 1 level (to a maximum of 8th level when you reach 20th level).

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Living Vessel](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=188)

</column>

---

The more you try to force your body to stay yours, the more it warps to channel the energy flowing through you. Whether you grow horns to match the wild hunt fey within you, develop a claw like that of the treachery demon sharing your soul, or feel a tentacle rip out of you from the outer being that imprinted itself on your psyche, the entity within you refuses to be contained. You gain an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack of your choice with its type determined by your entity. It deals 1d6 damage of a damage type appropriate for the unarmed attack (such as bludgeoning for the tentacle). This unarmed attack is in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) weapon group and has the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170), [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179), and [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103) traits.

    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Entourage](/Feats.aspx?ID=1066) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 72

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6); [Hobnobber](/Feats.aspx?ID=791)

</column>

---

You have a small group of admirers who tend to follow you around while you’re in civilized settlements. Your admirers are helpful to you, allowing you to make simple [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) of them such as purchasing basic equipment with your funds or finding a room at an inn. These admirers do not travel with you to places that are obviously dangerous, including most adventure locations, but they’ll wait for you at the nearest settlement. Your admirers never use actions in encounter mode other than to retreat, and they abandon you if you intentionally bring them harm or at the GM’s discretion. When you [Gather Information](/Actions.aspx?ID=49), you can use your admirers to assist you, granting a +1 circumstance bonus to your Diplomacy check and reducing the time it takes even further (typically to 30 minutes, rather than 1 hour with the Hobnobber feat alone). If you have the [Sow Rumor](/Feats.aspx?ID=1065) feat, you can have your admirers assist you, with the same benefits as Gather Information.

<title level="2">Firebrand Options</title>

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 71

The Firebrands use a variety of unorthodox equipment and techniques to achieve their goals, whether those goals include drawing attention, or subterfuge and subtlety. The following Firebrand options are uncommon, and members of the Firebrands gain access to them once they reach the rank of second mark. The [Entourage](/Feats.aspx?ID=1066) feat is rare even for members of the Firebrands, as it requires a certain degree of fame and in-world activity to acquire, and potentially requires the player or GM to keep track of additional background NPCs. Typically, only third mark and fourth mark Firebrands have the notoriety and social influence required to maintain an entourage. While Firebrands seek to build an entourage more than most adventurers, it’s not unreasonable for any famous character to gain access to it if the players are interested in playing with the [Entourage](/Feats.aspx?ID=1066) feat.

**Related Feats**: [Backup Disguise](/Feats.aspx?ID=1064), [Sow Rumor](/Feats.aspx?ID=1065)

[Entreat with Forebears](/Feats.aspx?ID=1812) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Sorcerer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=148" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 139

**Prerequisites**
a bloodline that corresponds with a creature trait

</column>

---

Something about your presence causes creatures of your bloodline to, consciously or not, recognize you as one of their own, and you become inured to their tricks. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6), [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5), and [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks when interacting with creatures that have the trait corresponding to your bloodline, and you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Perception and saving throws against such creatures. For example, an [aberrant bloodline](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=1) sorcerer would gain this benefit against creatures with the [aberration](/Traits.aspx?ID=1) trait. The GM is the final arbiter of which creatures match your bloodline.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Fists of the Ruby Phoenix</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Monk" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=112" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #166: Despair on Danger Island](/Sources.aspx?ID=85) pg. 74

</column>

---

You can transform your inner power into a type of energy to empower your ki abilities. When you gain this feat, choose either acid, cold, electricity, fire, or sonic damage. When you cast [_ki blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=484), you can choose to have the spell deal the type of damage you chose instead of force damage. When you cast [_ki form_](/Spells.aspx?ID=738) or [_ki strike_](/Spells.aspx?ID=486), add the type of damage you chose to the list of damage types you can select for the spell.

**Special** At the GM's discretion, this feat can alter other ki spells.

<title level="2">Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #166: Despair on Danger Island](/Sources.aspx?ID=85) pg. 74

The player characters might learn some of these techniques from friends and rivals during their stay on Bonmu, allowing them to select the feats the next time they would gain a feat. Surviving combat against Syu Tak-nwa allows the characters to take the three witch feats, while defeating or impressing the Ahmoza twins allows them to take Entwined Energy Ki. Lighting the candles and praying in the temple of Irori's prayer room (area A8) gives them access to Wronged Monk's Wrath.

**Related Feats**: [Syu Tak-Nwa's Deadly Hair](/Feats.aspx?ID=2690), [Syu Tak-Nwa's Hexed Locks](/Feats.aspx?ID=2691), [Syu Tak-Nwa's Skillful Tresses](/Feats.aspx?ID=2689), [Wronged Monk's Wrath](/Feats.aspx?ID=2693)

You can rapidly adapt to climates and help others do the same. After an hour in an [environment](/Rules.aspx?ID=590) , you and up to five allies can treat the natural temperature effects of an environment as one step less severe (treat extreme cold as severe cold or extreme heat as severe heat, for instance). This reduction in severity is cumulative with any equipment (such as cold-weather gear) or spells (such as environmental endurance). If you're legendary in Survival, you may protect yourself and up to five allies, and you treat temperature effects as two steps less severe.

---

You step outside of the flow of time momentarily, allowing you to avoid dangers. Your physical form stops existing momentarily, and you can't be targeted or affected until the start of your next turn—you simply don't exist at that moment in time. Your turn ends immediately, advancing 1 round for all timed durations and effects, such as conditions and afflictions. You still attempt saving throws, flat checks, or any other checks at the end of your turn as normal, but you don't take any damage due to these checks (though you take any non-damaging effects as normal). At the start of your next turn, you reenter the flow of time and reappear in the same space where you left time last round. If the space isn't clear, you arrive in the nearest open space.

**Source** [Dark Archive (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=293) pg. 187

**Archetype** [Chronoskimmer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=349)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Chronoskimmer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8489)

**Trigger**
Your turn begins.

</column>

---

You step outside of the flow of time momentarily, allowing you to avoid dangers. Your physical form stops existing momentarily, and you can't be targeted or affected until the start of your next turn— you simply don't exist at that moment in time. Your turn ends immediately, advancing 1 round for all timed durations and effects, such as conditions and afflictions. You still attempt saving throws, flat checks, or any other checks at the end of your turn as normal, but you don't take any damage due to these checks (though you take any non-damaging effects as normal). At the start of your next turn, you reenter the flow of time and reappear in the same space where you left time last round. If the space isn't clear, you arrive in the nearest open space.

<traits>

<trait label="Oath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=119" />
</traits>

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 118

**Prerequisites**
[tenets of good](/Tenets.aspx?ID=1)

</column>

---

You've sworn an oath to slay the alien abominations that lurk in the remote corners of Golarion and prey on the weak. You gain following edict: “You must slay aberrations whose actions are in direct opposition to your deity’s edicts when you encounter them as long as you have a reasonable chance of success.”

 Your Retributive Strike gains a +4 circumstance bonus to damage against an aberration, or +6 if you have master proficiency with the weapon you used. Your Glimpse of Redemption’s resistance against damage from an aberration is 7 + your level. If you use Liberating Step triggered by an aberration, your ally gains a +4 circumstance bonus to checks granted by your Liberating Step, and the ally can Step twice afterward.

 You don’t consider aberrations whose actions are in direct opposition to your deity’s edicts to be legitimate authorities, even in nations they rule.

---

You keep a book of occult spells, similar to a wizard's [spellbook](/Equipment.aspx?ID=53), and can use its spells to supplement your spell repertoire. Add all the spells in your repertoire to this book for free. You can use the [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) skill to [Learn Spells](/Skills.aspx?General=true&ID=4) and add them to your spellbook by paying the appropriate cost, similar to a wizard.

 During your daily preparations, choose any one spell from your book of occult spells. If that spell is already in your spell repertoire, you can treat it as an additional signature spell that day. If it isn't in your repertoire, treat it as though it were until your next daily preparations.

Your link with your eidolon is so intense that you continuously reinforce its abilities. fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Eternal Guide](/Feats.aspx?ID=7152) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Animist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=836" />
<trait label="Apparition" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=837" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 26

**Frequency**
once per week

</column>

---

Your attuned apparitions recognize that you still have essential work to do and refuse to allow you to pass on, gathering up your essence to carry your soul back to the community you call home. Choose a single settlement with a population of at least 100 people. Whenever you die and are not returned to life within 24 hours by other means, as long as the settlement still exists and there are no other claims on your soul (such as a contract with a [devil](/Traits.aspx?ID=575)) and nothing trapping your soul (such as being slain by a critical hit from a [vilderavn](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3229)), your attuned apparition magically transports your soul, remains, and all of the items you had worn or carried at the time of your death (so long as they have not been otherwise recovered) back to the chosen settlement, where you are reborn. The nature of this rebirth varies between animists; some magically reconstitute and reinvigorate their physical forms to return to life in their original bodies, while others pass their knowledge and power on to a new inheritor who effectively takes their place in the grand story of existence. When returned to your original physical form in this manner, you are brought back in your physical prime, restored to youthful health and vigor. This effectively makes you immune to dying of old age so long as you are not killed by violence less than a week before you would have died of old age.

Regardless of the exact nature of your rebirth, you or your inheritor are fully restored with your level, experience, and equipment intact one week after your death. If you choose an inheritor and their ancestry is different than yours, your attribute scores do not change but you can freely retrain your ancestry feats and any other feats that relied on them as prerequisites as part of your rebirth.

There is no limit to the number of times you can be reborn, but if you die before a week has passed since your last rebirth, neither you nor your attuned apparitions have recovered enough energy to complete the process again, and your soul passes to whatever final reward it has earned.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs=""
>
[Eternal Hero](/Feats.aspx?ID=8165) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 79

**Archetype** [Heroic Scion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=339)

**Prerequisites**
[Heroic Scion Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=8151)

</column>

---

You might be protected by divine intervention or the necessity of cosmic balance. You might be watched over by agents of destiny or fate. You could even be simply someone whose luck and skill have always worked together to ensure your triumph, no matter the odds you might face. Whatever the explanation, you’re almost impossible to kill. You reduce the DC of [recovery checks](/Rules.aspx?ID=2326) by 1 (this is cumulative with the reduction from the Heroic Scion Dedication feat). Whenever your [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) condition would increase to 4 or more, it doesn’t increase. The first time each day you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points or outright killed by magical means, you instead remain at 1 Hit Point and become immune to all damage until the end of your next turn.

If you finally do die, you can spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) as a free action to immediately reincarnate—manifesting in a new body with the same statistics (save for potential changes to your ancestry and ancestry feats) within 15 feet of where your death occurred. Each time you repeat this reincarnation, the cost to do so increases by 1, so that after your third reincarnation, you can no longer swiftly return (as no mythic character can ever have more than 3 Mythic Points at one time).

Whatever the explanation, you’re almost impossible to kill. You reduce the DC of recovery checks by 1 (this is cumulative with the reduction from the Heroic Scion Dedication feat). Whenever your doomed condition would increase to 4 or more, it doesn’t increase. The first time each day you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points or outright killed by magical means, you instead remain at 1 Hit Point and become immune to all damage until the end of your next turn. If you finally do die, you can spend a Mythic Point as a free action to immediately reincarnate—manifesting in a new body with the same statistics (save for potential changes to your ancestry and ancestry feats) within 15 feet of where your death occurred. Each time you repeat this reincarnation, the cost to do so increases by 1, so that after your third reincarnation, you can no longer swiftly return (as no mythic character can ever have more than 3 Mythic Points at one time).

[Eternal Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7374) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Destiny" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=838" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 127

**Archetype** [Eternal Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=292)

</column>

---

As your renown as a fighter grows, your Calling comes to fruition. Almost nothing can keep you down. During your [daily preparations](/Rules.aspx?ID=2575), choose [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61), [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68), or [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71). For the remainder of the day, when you roll a success against an effect that would impose that condition on you, you get a critical success instead. In addition, anytime you gain the chosen condition, reduce its value by 1. You can change the chosen condition with a single action that has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561) trait.

<title level="2">Eternal Legend Dedication leads to...</title>
[Death from Above](/Feats.aspx?ID=7380), [Demolishing Knockback](/Feats.aspx?ID=7375), [Earth to Heavens Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7376), [Exaltation Overwhelming](/Feats.aspx?ID=7385), [Fautless Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=7377), [Fight Through Oblivion](/Feats.aspx?ID=7389), [Finish Their Story!](/Feats.aspx?ID=7390), [Immovable Object](/Feats.aspx?ID=7378), [Leaping Hedgehog Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=7381), [Legend of Combat](/Feats.aspx?ID=7386), [Living Epic](/Feats.aspx?ID=7391), [Mythic Weapon Specialization](/Feats.aspx?ID=7387), [Pierce The Eye](/Feats.aspx?ID=7382), [Scattering Shout](/Feats.aspx?ID=7379), [Terrifying Mien](/Feats.aspx?ID=7383), [Weft and Warp](/Feats.aspx?ID=7384)

[Eternal Torch](/Feats.aspx?ID=4237) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Impulse" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=502" />
<trait label="Kineticist" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=504" />
<trait label="Light" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=100" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 28

</column>

---

You open a connection to your kinetic gate, large enough for a torch flame to flow. You create a magical, [torch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=60)-like flame within 120 feet in any color you choose. It's as bright and hot as a torch. You can have it orbit a target willing creature or emit from a target object that's unattended or attended by a willing creature. If you create a flame on a weapon, you still need to use it as an [improvised weapon](/Rules.aspx?ID=224) to attack with the flame, just as with a torch.

 The flame has an unlimited duration. You can have a maximum number of Eternal Torches equal to your Constitution modifier, and you can Dismiss each torch individually.

---
**Level (8th)** All your torches—even ones you already created— shed [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 60-foot radius (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 60 feet).

    right="Feat 18"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Eternity-Incinerating Blaze](/Feats.aspx?ID=7189) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Exemplar" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=839" />
<trait label="Ikon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=840" />
<trait label="Void" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=510" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 42

**Usage**
imbued into a weapon ikon

</column>

---

The blaze of your divine spark is hot enough that it burns in not just the present, but the past and future as well. Whenever you score a critical hit with the imbued ikon, the target becomes doomed 1 or increases its doomed condition by 1. If the target’s maximum dying value is reduced to 0 by this ability, it immediately dies in a flash of spiritual fire that reduces its body to ash. This effect applies even when the ikon is not empowered. The ikon also gains the following transcendence ability.

**Transcendence—Burn out of Time** <actions string="Two Actions" /> (spirit, transcendence, void) An impossible amount of energy blazes in a sphere above you before compressing itself into your weapon. Strike one creature. The Strike deals an additional 3d8 spirit damage and 3d8 void damage. If the creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it’s immediately killed and reduced to ash, not in the present, but in the recent past, erasing the consequences of their recent actions. If a creature died within the last round as a result of the incinerated target’s actions, that creature is returned to life with 5d8 Hit Points at the location that it died as its death is retroactively undone.

[Ever Dreaming](/Feats.aspx?ID=3882) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 207

**Archetype** [Sleepwalker](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=195)

**Prerequisites**
[Sleepwalker Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3873)

</column>

---

You draw no distinction between the sleeping and waking worlds. Your [Daydream Trance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3873) has an unlimited duration, and you no longer need to take an action to enter it. If you're [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) due to sleep, you don't take the –4 penalty to AC, Perception, and Reflex saves, and don't have the [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) condition. You're still [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1) while asleep. You can act on your turn while asleep, though you're [slowed 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) until you fully awaken.

---

Your eidolon has enhanced senses. It gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception, and can't be flanked except by creatures that are higher level than it. It can see [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) creatures and objects; they appear translucent and are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4). When your eidolon moves within 30 feet of an [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92) that can be [disbelieved](/Rules.aspx?ID=267), the GM rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) check to disbelieve it, even if your eidolon didn't spend an action to Interact.

>
[Everdistant Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=2747) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Fists of the Ruby Phoenix</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Champion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=24" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #168: King of the Mountain](/Sources.aspx?ID=87) pg. 75

**Trigger**
A creature within your aura is targeted by a ranged attack or a creature moves through your aura.

**Requirements**
You have at least one [aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206) from a champion feat or feature.

</column>

---

The spatial barrier of Syndara's Island has taught you that distance can foil enemies better than any armor. You warp space, causing each square within your aura that the attack or creature would move through to count as triple the distance. If this reaction is used on a ranged attack, the attack takes range increment penalties based on the adjusted range and fails if this would cause it to exceed its maximum range.

<title level="2">Capstone Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #168: King of the Mountain](/Sources.aspx?ID=87) pg. 75

Player characters can select one of the following new class feats for their 20th-level class feat upon entering the _Glass Lighthouse_ or by meditating on the cushion in area H4.

**Related Feats**: [All the Time in the World](/Feats.aspx?ID=2744), [Dance of Intercession](/Feats.aspx?ID=2745), [Demon's Hair](/Feats.aspx?ID=2746), [Extradimensional Stash](/Feats.aspx?ID=2748), [Head of the Night Parade](/Feats.aspx?ID=2749), [Heart of the Kaiju](/Feats.aspx?ID=2750), [Plum Deluge](/Feats.aspx?ID=2751), [Ruby Resurrection](/Feats.aspx?ID=2752), [Scapegoat Parallel Self](/Feats.aspx?ID=2753), [Sever Space](/Feats.aspx?ID=2754), [Time Dilation Cascade](/Feats.aspx?ID=2755), [Vitality-Manipulating Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=2756), [Vivacious Afterimage](/Feats.aspx?ID=2757), [Whirlwind Toss](/Feats.aspx?ID=2758), [Worldsphere Gravity](/Feats.aspx?ID=2759)

---

You brace your shield with both hands, enhancing its potential for both offense and defense. When in this stance, you wield the shield with both hands. When wielding a shield this way, increase the weapon damage die of the shield’s boss or spikes by one step, and increase the shield’s Hardness by 2 when using the [Shield Block](/Feats.aspx?ID=839) reaction.

Those with both the champion and fighter traits are both champion class feats and fighter class feats; when you take one of these feats, it loses the trait that doesn’t apply to your class.

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 90

**Archetypes** [Bastion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=240) (Level 6), [Bastion](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=49) (Level 6)

**Prerequisites**
[Everstand Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=1087)

**Access**
A character who is a member of the Knights of Lastwall has access to this option.

**Requirements**
You are wielding a shield in two hands.

</column>

---

Your follow-up blow leaves you an opening to set your shield. Make a Strike with the wielded shield. If the Strike hits and deals damage, you also [Raise your Shield](/Actions.aspx?ID=98).

<title level="2">Knights of Lastwall Class Feats</title>

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 90

The following class feats are available to Knights of Lastwall. Those with the champion trait are champion class feats. Those with both the champion and fighter traits are both champion class feats and fighter class feats; when you take one of these feats, it loses the trait that doesn’t apply to your class.

**Related Feats**: [Everstand Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=1087), [Impassable Wall Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=1091), [Light of Revelation](/Feats.aspx?ID=1089), [Sun Blade](/Feats.aspx?ID=1090)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Everyday Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6930) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Tanuki" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=830" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 66

</column>

---

There’s nothing better than being a tanuki, but sometimes you need a less conspicuous form when going into the big city or other crowded places. When you [Change Shape](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=90), you can assume the form of a common Small or Medium [humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=628) ancestry prevalent where you grew up, typically human. This everyday form is a specific form with the same age and body type as your true tanuki form and has roughly analogous physical traits, such as hair color.

<title level="2">Everyday Form leads to...</title>
[False Priest Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=6935), [Many Faces](/Feats.aspx?ID=6940)

    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Everyone Duck!](/Feats.aspx?ID=1128) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=12) pg. 112

**Archetype** [Pathfinder Agent](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=13)

**Prerequisites**
[Pathfinder Agent Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=871)

**Access**
A character who is a member of the Pathfinder Society has access to this option.

**Trigger**
You fail, but don’t critically fail, an attempt to [Disable a Device](/Actions.aspx?ID=69) on a trap.

</column>

---

You intentionally set off the trap, but you take special precautions to protect yourself and your allies from the trap’s effects. For the next 2 rounds, if the trap rolls a critical success on an attack roll, it gets a normal success instead, and if anyone rolls a critical failure on their saving throw against the trap, they get a normal failure instead.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Everyone's a Suspect](/Feats.aspx?ID=1481) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Investigator" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=318" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 65

</column>

---

You are so suspicious of everyone you meet that you keep mental notes on how to defeat them all—even your own allies. After interacting with a creature for at least 1 minute, you automatically [Pursue a Lead](/Actions.aspx?ID=544) with that creature as the subject. You can have any number of such leads at any given time, and when you Pursue a Lead again, you don't give up any of these automatic subjects.

>
[Exaltation Overwhelming](/Feats.aspx?ID=7385) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Emotion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=590" />
<trait label="Fear" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=598" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=647" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
<trait label="Visual" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=727" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 128

**Archetype** [Eternal Legend](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=292)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Eternal Legend Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=7374)

</column>

---

Raising your weapon or fist aloft, you begin to gleam with dazzling radiance. You fulminate with power and glory, making it clear to all who see you that your legend is real and possibly even greater than purported. Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320).  All enemies who can see you must succeed at a Will saving throw against your class DC or become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 3 (frightened 4 on a critical failure). You and any ally who can see you may choose to [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) or [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=2305) as a free action. Any of these Strikes are made at mythic proficiency.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 277

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You improve your exalted reaction with the benefit listed for your cause.

**Desecration** While you have the benefit, you also gain a +2 status bonus to saving throws against effects created by enemies in your champion’s aura.

**Grandeur** Any [_revealing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1653) created by your Flash of Grandeur lasts for 1 minute.

**Iniquity** The damage dealt to enemies other than the triggering creatures increases by an amount equal to the damage dice of Destructive Vengeance (apply this after you halve the damage).

**Justice** The penalty is –2 instead of –5. 

**Liberation** You and all affected allies can attempt to break free, not just the triggering ally.

**Obedience** The damage dealt to creatures other than the triggering creature who refuse to drop prone increases to half the damage the triggering creature would take (roll the damage only once for all affected creatures). 

**Redemption** The resistance isn’t reduced.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Execution](/Feats.aspx?ID=3338) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Vigilante" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=326" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Night of the Gray Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=99) pg. 65

**Archetype** [Gray Gardener](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=124)

**Prerequisites**
[Harsh Judgment](/Feats.aspx?ID=3330); [Vigilante Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2083); member of the Gray Gardeners

**Requirements**
You have condemned a foe with [Harsh Judgment.](/Feats.aspx?ID=3330)

</column>

---

You swing wide, attempting to behead your condemned foe. Make a melee Strike against your condemned foe. If you hit, your condemned foe takes 8d6 extra precision damage with a basic Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. If the condemned foe is reduced to 0 Hit Points by the execution and requires a head to live, they die. For creatures with multiple heads, this usually kills the creature only if you sever its last head. The creature then becomes temporarily immune to your Execution for 1 day.

fields.markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Exorcist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3454) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 22

**Archetype** [Exorcist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=171)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

You've learned to attract, quell, and purify spirits, housing them in a special receptacle called a _spirit dwelling_ until they're ready to move on. Through the power of prayers or ritual incantations, one mundane object in your possession becomes a _spirit dwelling_. Your _spirit dwelling_ functions as a lure for lost spirits weakened by their time on the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1). Each day during your daily preparations, your _spirit dwelling_ attracts a spirit wisp who comes to dwell inside. If your _spirit dwelling_ contains no wisps, you can spend 10 minutes in a minor ritual to cast your _spirit dwelling_ around an area and attract another wisp. You can also capture stronger spirit remnants from vanquished [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) spirits, as explained in the [Spirit Dwellings and Remnants](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=171) sidebar. As long as your _spirit dwelling_ contains any spirits, it glows faintly, casting dim light in a 10-foot radius.

 As an exorcist, you do more than just collect spirits: you also help rid them of their burdens and lingering resentments, aiding their transition from the Material Plane. Every day, before your daily preparations, any spirit wisps and remnants remaining within your _spirit dwelling_ from the previous day are purified and can join the River of Souls in their final journey to [Pharasma's](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=15).

 You can also learn abilities that let you purify a spirit in your _spirit dwelling_ immediately in a cathartic surge, granting you a helpful effect as they depart for the afterlife. Any actions you gain from the exorcist archetype gain either the [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) or [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) trait, depending on whether you used Occultism or Religion to qualify for Exorcist Dedication.

 Spirit's Mercy is the simplest of the purifications.

 **Spirit's Mercy** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) **Trigger** You take [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128) or [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118) damage, or you take any type of damage caused by a [haunt](/Traits.aspx?ID=88), [ghost](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51), or other [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) undead; **Cost** 1 spirit wisp or remnant; **Effect** You purify a spirit by having it perform a final act of mercy to lessen the damage caused by another spirit. This grants you resistance to positive and negative damage (or resistance to all damage if caused by a haunt or incorporeal undead) against the triggering effect. If you expend a spirit wisp, the resistance is equal to twice your level. If you expend a spirit remnant, the resistance is equal to three times the level of the incorporeal undead or haunt from which you gained the remnant.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the exorcist archetype.

<title level="2">Exorcist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Cast Out](/Feats.aspx?ID=3455), [Enticing Dwelling](/Feats.aspx?ID=3458), [Spirit's Absolution](/Feats.aspx?ID=3456), [Spirit's Anguish](/Feats.aspx?ID=3457)

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Player Core 2](/Sources.aspx?ID=227) pg. 67

**Archetype** [Demolitionist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=365) (Level 12)

</column>

---

You can throw bombs at just the right trajectory to create especially large and powerful explosions. When you throw an [alchemical bomb](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=7) and that bomb has the [splash](/Traits.aspx?ID=699) trait, you can have the splash damage affect all creatures within 10 feet of the target instead of 5 feet. If you do, you gain a status bonus to the bomb's splash damage equal to your Intelligence modifier. If you have the [bomber](/ResearchFields.aspx?ID=5) 5th-level field discovery, this additional damage applies even if you caused your bomb to deal splash damage equal to your Intelligence modifier instead of the normal amount, allowing your bombs to deal splash damage equal to double your Intelligence modifier.

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 43

**Prerequisites**
[Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755)

</column>

---

You can blast the energy of a spell out around the target of your attack. When you [Spellstrike](/Actions.aspx?ID=755) with a spell that has an area of a [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385), [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386), or [line](/Rules.aspx?ID=2388), the spell creates an area instead of affecting only the target. The target must be in the area. A burst is centered on a corner of the target’s square; if the target is Large or larger, the burst use the square corner closest to the center of the target and choose the corner if more than one is eligible. A cone or line emits from you and must include the target; if you’re not adjacent to the target (using a [reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=684) weapon or [starlit span](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=4), for example), choose any square adjacent to the target as the source. The spell affects all creatures in the area as normal, but the Strike still targets only one creature.

</column>

---

You have a system that lets you search at great speed, finding details and secrets twice as quickly as others can. When Searching, you take half as long as usual to Search a given area. This means that while exploring, you double the Speed you can move while ensuring you’ve Searched an area before walking into it (up to half your Speed). If you’re legendary in Perception, you instead Search areas four times as quickly.

---

Your followers' skills have developed over the course of your  adventures. All your followers become [experienced followers.](/Followers.aspx)  

Additionally, your followers have grown accustomed to the perils of battle, developing the confidence to attack foes  without your direction. During an encounter, even if you don't use the [Direct Follower](/Actions.aspx?ID=3453) action, your active follower spend can still use 1 action that round on your turn to Stride or Strike. They can do this at any point during your turn, as long as you aren't currently taking an action. If they do, that's all the actions they get that round—you can't Direct them later.

---

You often smuggle things past the authorities. When the GM rolls your Stealth check to see if a passive observer notices a small item you’ve concealed, the GM uses the number rolled or 10—whichever is higher—as the result of your die roll, adding it to your Stealth modifier to determine your Stealth check result. If you’re a master in Stealth, the GM uses the number rolled or 15, and if you’re legendary in Stealth, you automatically succeed at hiding a small concealed item from passive observers. This provides no benefits when a creature attempts a Perception check while actively searching you for hidden items.
