    right="Feat 9"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Expert Longevity](/Feats.aspx?ID=22) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Elf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=58" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 41

**Prerequisites**
[Ancestral Longevity](/Feats.aspx?ID=12)

</column>

---

You’ve continued to refine the knowledge and skills you’ve gained through your life. When you choose a skill in which to become trained with [Ancestral Longevity](/Feats.aspx?ID=12), you can also choose a skill in which you are already trained and become an expert in that skill. This lasts until your Ancestral Longevity expires.

 When the effects of Ancestral Longevity and Expert Longevity expire, you can retrain one of your skill increases. The skill increase you gain from this retraining must either make you trained in the skill you chose with Ancestral Longevity or make you an expert in the skill you chose with Expert Longevity.

<title level="2">Expert Longevity leads to...</title>
[Universal Longevity](/Feats.aspx?ID=23)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Exploding Bullet](/Feats.aspx?ID=9055) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Magus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=953" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=355) pg. 19

**Prerequisites**
[volatile spark hybrid study](/HybridStudies.aspx?ID=16)

**Requirements**
You’re wielding an unloaded [firearm](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=16).

</column>

---

You load your gun with a bullet forged of magic instead of matter, barely contained in an arcane shell. [Interact](/Actions.aspx?ID=2297) to [reload](/Rules.aspx?ID=2196) your firearm, creating an arcane round made from your choice of [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) or [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697) energy. When you shoot this round, the Strike gains the [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534) trait and the corresponding energy trait. The firearm gains the [scatter 5 feet](/Traits.aspx?ID=848) trait, or gains a +1 status bonus to its splash damage if it already has the scatter trait. The scatter trait’s splash damage uses the energy type you chose. The bullet disappears if not fired by the end of your next turn.

If your firearm takes more than 1 action to reload, you need to use Exploding Bullet for all the actions needed to reload it to get the benefits.

**Special** When you use volatile spark’s Reloading Cascade action, you can use Exploding Bullet instead of an Interact action to reload a firearm.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Spellshape" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=513" />

**Source** [Player Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=216) pg. 203

Your summoned creature appears in a detonation of arcane runes. If your next action is to Cast a Spell with the summon trait, all creatures in a 10-foot emanation around the creature you summoned take 1d4 fire damage per spell rank. If the creature summoned has the acid, cold, electricity, sonic, or spirit trait, you can deal damage of that type instead.

**Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 118 **Prerequisites** [Blazing Talon Surge](/Feats.aspx?ID=2270) **Requirements** You are in [Rain of Embers Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=2269) and have a target [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33). --- You lift your enemy into the air before bringing them crashing down with a fiery detonation. Roll an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check against your target's Fortitude DC. You take a –1 circumstance penalty to your check if the target is one size larger than you and a –3 circumstance penalty if it's larger than that. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your check if the target is one size smaller than you and a +3 circumstance bonus if it's smaller than that. **Critical Success** The target takes 12d6 fire damage and falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) in an unoccupied adjacent square of your choice. The target is no longer grabbed. The target and any creature adjacent to it also each take 1d6 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29).
**Success** As critical success, but the target takes 6d6 fire damage instead of 12d6, and creatures don't take persistent fire damage.
**Failure** The target is no longer grabbed.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but you fall prone. Rain of Embers Style **Source** [PFS Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=50) pg. 118 The martial artist Meleeka Sanvara (CN female human monk) originally met agents of the Pathfinder Society as an enemy when the agents were sent to retrieve an artifact she had stolen. Now, Meleeka works as a Pathfinder agent and occasionally shares the knowledge of her family's unique martial arts techniques with agents who earn her trust. **Related Feats**: [Blazing Talon Surge](/Feats.aspx?ID=2270), [Rain of Embers Stance](/Feats.aspx?ID=2269)

    pfs="Restricted"
>
[Explosive Entry](/Feats.aspx?ID=3242) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 133

**Archetype** [Demolitionist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=118)

**Prerequisites**
[Demolitionist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3240); Master in [Engineering Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8)

</column>

---

You know exactly how to make a memorable entrance... by detonating a [bomb](/Equipment.aspx?Category=6&Subcategory=7) to produce a devastating explosion, of course! You [Set Explosives](/Feats.aspx?ID=3240) on a door, window, container, or heavy gate. When the explosives detonate, you can attempt an Engineering Lore check to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34) the target. If a bomb would add an item bonus to attack rolls, add that item bonus to your Engineering Lore check. Since you're blasting your way in, you can't avoid breaking the object or structure. If you roll a critical success, you get a success instead.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Explosive Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=3045) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Fire" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=72" />
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
<trait label="Move" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=114" />
<trait label="Unstable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=416" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 24

</column>

---

You aim an explosion from your innovation downward to launch yourself into the air. You jump up to 30 feet in any direction without touching the ground. You must land on a space of solid ground, or else you fall after using your next action. As normal for effects where you fall after using your next action, you still fall at the end of your turn, even if you don't use any further actions that turn.

**Special** If your innovation is a [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109), it can take this action rather than you.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Explosive Maneuver](/Feats.aspx?ID=3078) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Inventor" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=408" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 30

**Prerequisites**
[weapon innovation](/Innovations.aspx?ID=3)

**Requirements**
Your last action was a successful Strike against a foe using your weapon innovation.

</column>

---

Thanks to a hidden experimental feature you built into your weapon, your weapon explosively deploys levers, tangling hooks, or similar mechanisms to provide significant assistance when you perform a combat maneuver. When you use Explosive Maneuver, choose [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35), [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38), or [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40). Your weapon innovation must have a weapon trait that matches the action you chose (for instance, to choose Grapple, your weapon must have the [grapple](/Traits.aspx?ID=184) trait). You take the chosen action against the same foe as your previous successful Strike, using the same multiple attack penalty as your previous successful Strike. You still increase your multiple attack penalty after the Grapple, Shove, or Trip, as normal.

You use additional primal energy to transform, creating a burst of elemental energy to complement your transformation. If your next action is to cast a non-cantrip [morph](/Traits.aspx?ID=657) or [polymorph](/Traits.aspx?ID=670) spell, select acid, cold, electricity, or fire. </traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**
[Trick Driver Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3140)

</column>

---

You can optimize your [vehicle's](/Vehicles.aspx) performance, coaxing extra speed and choosing paths to avoid slowdowns. When calculating your travel speed for the day while piloting a vehicle, you can attempt a [Driving Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) check to increase your vehicle's travel speed. The DC is determined by the GM but is typically based on the vehicle's piloting DC or a difficulty based on the environment, whichever is harder. On a success, increase your vehicle's travel speed by half. This has no effect on your vehicle's movement in encounters.

---

Your face is constructed to move organically and show your emotions, making you more relatable to organic creatures. You become trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39). If you are already trained in Diplomacy, you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. Additionally, you gain the [Glad-Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=5153) skill feat, even if you do not meet its prerequisites.

**Enhancement** You are particularly skilled at pouring your heart out to others. You gain the Plaintive Plea action. 

**Plaintive Plea** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You make an emotional appeal to convince someone during a diplomatic encounter. If your next activity is to attempt a Diplomacy check to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) or [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393), or to attempt to influence a creature during an [influence encounter](/Rules.aspx?ID=3040), you can roll twice and take the better result.

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 20 **Prerequisites** [Base Kinesis](/Actions.aspx?ID=2126) --- You've refined the control you can exert over your elements. Add the following options to Base Kinesis.
  • **Proliferate** You cause an existing element to expand. This works like the generate option, except that you can either create an equal quantity of the element in the same square as its source or in an adjacent square, or cause the element to expand to fill its square (making a flame bigger or turning a twig into a small tree, for example). After you proliferate an element, it reacts to the environment naturally—water you proliferated into thin air would splash back down, for example. This affects only natural forms of the element, not durable, crafted goods.
  • **Regulate** (air, fire, metal, or water only) You change the temperature of an existing element, making it colder or warmer. This can snuff out a flame or turn water to ice or steam. After this change, the element cools or warms naturally unless you Sustain the impulse. An item that gets cold or hot enough (as determined by the GM) can be used as an improvised weapon that deals 1 cold damage or 1 fire damage in addition to the damage the GM determines for the improvised weapon.
  • **Sculpt** (earth, metal, or wood only) Reshape an existing element into a small object of a design you choose. It looks crude and artificial on close examination. The sculpted element can be shaped into a functional short tool (or a long tool if your Base Kinesis can affect 1 Bulk or greater). It's too fragile and artificial to be used as a weapon or have any monetary value.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Darkness" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=39" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Fetchling" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=300" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Ancestry Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=74) pg. 86

**Frequency**
once every 10 minutes

</column>

---

You wrap shadow around a single unattended light source within 120 feet that's no larger than a torch. Any non-magical light source you target is automatically extinguished. For magical light sources, attempt a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check using your Fortitude or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) modifier against the target's DC. Your counteract level is equal to half your level rounded up. Successfully counteracting the light source suppresses its ability to produce light for 1 minute, but not any other effects. If you're in dim light or darkness when you Extinguish Light, its range is 240 feet.

<traits>

[Unbreakable Goblin](/Heritages.aspx?ID=20) heritage

</column>

---

Your rubbery physique makes it easier for you to wedge yourself into tight spaces and more difficult for your enemies to dislodge you. You become trained in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1). If you would automatically become trained in Acrobatics (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. If you roll a success to [Squeeze](/Actions.aspx?ID=31), you get a critical success instead. While you're Squeezing, you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DCs against attempts to [Shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) you or otherwise move you from your space.

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 39 _[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) When using Exact Vow of Nonviolence on an unattended item, the DC is a standard DC for the item's level._ --- You entice or threaten a weapon, making it swear not to harm you. Attempt a [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) check to [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) or an [Intimidation](/Actions.aspx?ID=2393) check to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395) against one weapon within 60 feet—even though most weapons are inanimate and mindless, your words somehow still can affect it as if it were living and you shared a language. The DC for this check is the Will DC of the creature wielding the weapon or a moderate DC for the weapon's level if it's unattended. If the weapon is an intelligent item, use its Will DC. Regardless of the result of the save, the weapon is then temporarily immune to Extract Vow of Nonviolence for 1 day. **Special** When you gain this feat, choose cold iron, duskwood, dawnsilver, or silver. For some reason—perhaps because you underestimate this material, or because you think it a friend—you are forever unable to use Extract Vow of Nonviolence on objects composed of the chosen material. **Critical Success** The object swears not to hurt you. You gain [resistance](/Rules.aspx?ID=2318) to all damage dealt by that specific weapon as the weapon attempts to mitigate harm to you. The resistance is equal to half your level and lasts for 10 minutes.
**Success** As critical success, but the remaining duration decreases by 1 minute each time the weapon hits you (even if it deals no damage).

</column>

---

When you perform sleight of hand, you fold space so that objects really do disappear. You create a small extradimensional space somewhere within in your clothing that can hold up to 5 Bulk worth of objects. The space functions as a [_bag of holding_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=249), but can hold only up to 5 Bulk, has no Bulk of its own, and can be Interacted with using only one hand.

 In addition, when you [Palm an Object](/Actions.aspx?ID=67), you can place it directly into this extradimensional space as long as the space has sufficient free space to hold the object.

---

Most of the changes from the demon within you have harmed you so far, but you've found a way to expel some of the corruption within you to poison others. Until the beginning of your next turn, you and your weapons are covered in toxic sludge or another similar manifestation of the demonic corruption; your melee Strikes deal an additional 1d6 poison damage, and each time a creature hits you with a melee [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack or otherwise touches you, it takes 1d6 poison damage.

 At 14th level, the poison damage increases to 2d6, and at 20th level, the poison damage increases to 3d6.

<title

>
[Eye for Numbers](/Feats.aspx?ID=2127) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 206

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=14)

</column>

---

You've learned to subitize, quickly estimating the number of items in a group with relative accuracy at only a glance. You immediately learn the number of visually similar items in a group you can see (such as coins, books, or people), rounded to the first digit in the total number. For example, you could look at a case of potion vials and learn that it held about 30 vials, but you wouldn't know that it was exactly 33 vials, how many different types of potions there were, or how many of which type. Similarly, you could look at a pile of 2,805 coins and know that there were about 3,000 coins in all. You can use this ability only on items that can typically be counted, so you can't use it on grains of sand or stars in the sky, for example.

 In addition, when you attempt to [Decipher Writing](/Actions.aspx?ID=22) that is primarily numerical or mathematical, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your check.

Your time checking seemingly innocent cargo ships for illicit goods has made you as canny as you are suspicious. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to locate hidden panels, secret doors or hatches, [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) objects, and similar items (at the GM's discretion). If you aren't using the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=2301) action or [Search](/Actions.aspx?ID=2630), the GM automatically rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=690) check for you to notice these types of objects when you pass within 10 feet of them.

You know good artisanship when you see it and can wax poetic about crafting techniques and forms. You become trained in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) and gain a +1 circumstance bonus on all Crafting checks made to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26). In addition, you gain the [Crafter's Appraisal](/Feats.aspx?ID=2118) skill feat, enabling you to identify magic items using the Crafting skill.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Eye of the Arclords](/Feats.aspx?ID=870) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [World Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=6) pg. 81, [Wake the Dead #2](/Sources.aspx?ID=207) pg. 28

**Frequency**
once per day;

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2); [Arcane Sense](/Feats.aspx?ID=754)

**Access**
 You are a member of the Arclords of Nex.

</column>

---

You open an incandescent third eye upon your forehead. The eye can remain open for 1 minute, and you can close it before then with a single action with the concentrate trait. It can remain open for 2 minutes if you’re a master in Arcana, or 5 minutes if you’re legendary. While the eye is open, you gain the following benefits: you gain the effects of the [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66) arcane innate spell from your Arcane Sense at the start of each of your turns without needing to cast the spell; you gain [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415); you gain a +2 status bonus to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) undetected and hidden creatures and to your Perception DC against [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) and [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63). After your third eye closes, you are [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=7) for an amount of time equal to how long you had it open.
